The most notable is the open 6th District, where Republican Micah Quinney Jones will face Koh, who was backed by former President Joe Biden, former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, alongside several other alumni of the Biden administration. The support gave Koh a powerful establishment coalition in the crowded contest to succeed Moulton.
Micah Jones, candidate for Congress in Massachusetts, left, pictured alongside the U.S. Capitol Building, right. (Micah Jones for Congress; Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
Following Koh's win, Democratic National Committee Chairman Ken Martin congratulated the former Biden administration aide.

"From Boston City Hall and the U.S. Department of Labor to the White House, Dan Koh has dedicated his life to public service and ensuring government actually delivers for working families. He is a Massachusetts native who knows how to bring people together to solve problems and fight for our communities," Martin said in a statement. "In Congress, Dan will prioritize bringing down costs, protecting healthcare, making housing more affordable, strengthening workers’ rights, rooting out corruption, and holding Donald Trump accountable. The DNC is ready to work alongside him to make life more affordable for people throughout Massachusetts’ 6th Congressional District."
Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

title: Money trail exposes far-left shadow orgs pushing data center backlash as part of broader 'playbook': experts
summary: Climate activists and groups like Public Citizen and the Sierra Club are fueling data center opposition across the United States with progressive funding.
story: Fox News Digital spoke to Power The Future’s Larry Behrens about the left wing groups backing data center opposition and their reasons for doing so.

As the development of data centers continues to grow into one of the top hot button political issues in the United States, some experts are sounding the alarm on the various left-wing groups and climate activists who are pouring money and resources into data center opposition campaigns.
"It's a playbook we've seen before," Larry Behrens, communications director at Power The Future, told Fox News Digital in an interview.

"I think Americans saw this with the Dakota Access Pipeline. They see this with oil or natural gas production within the United States. This seemingly grassroots organization pops up, but yet they're all wearing the same T-shirts. They're all singing the same playbook, and they're only carrying the same signs, and so when we see that, we see that that's not really a grassroots organization that money is coming from somewhere, and in this case, against data centers."

Several left-wing organizations backing data center opposition have benefited from major progressive funding networks, including Public Citizen, which has listed George Soros’ Open Society Foundations among foundations whose "generous support" makes its work possible, and the Sierra Club, which received $3.6 million from Arabella Advisors’ Sixteen Thirty Fund between 2014 and 2022.
TOP ENERGY GROUP WARNS WEALTHY FOREIGNERS ARE POTENTIALLY BANKROLLING ANTI-DATA CENTER CAMPAIGNS ACROSS US
A crowd demonstrating against global warming and plastic pollution, concepts about green ecology and environmental sustainability. (Getty Images)

CodePink, which has targeted data center projects, has received funding linked to socialist megadonor Neville Roy Singham, who has deep ties to the Chinese Communist Party. Fox News Digital previously reported that Singham funneled roughly $285 million into six activist nonprofits, as the U.S. and China battle for global AI dominance.

In Texas, viewed by many as the front line of the data center fight, opposition has been fueled by a network of left-wing groups, including Public Citizen, the Sierra Club and the Party for Socialism and Liberation. Public Citizen is a founding member of the Texas Data Center Rebellion, which brought activists from across the state together for a two-day convening in San Antonio, while the Sierra Club’s Austin chapter, PSL and Save Our Springs Alliance teamed up for a July "Defend Dog’s Head" forum opposing a massive Austin development that includes data centers.

Several of the groups actively involved in fueling anti-ICE protests and "No Kings" protests across the country are also involved in pushing back against data centers. Earlier this year, Fox News Digital reported that Power the Future, a pro-energy advocacy group, sent a letter asking Congress to take a closer look at opposition to data centers springing up across the country, pointing out the various left-wing groups that were backing those efforts.

"What they do is they send their money through a maze of organizations, deliberately trying to mask what it is being used for and seeing that the tentacles reach in from far and are made to look local," Behrens explained. "Now, to be clear, there is local opposition and there are legitimate questions to ask, but when the legislative language is the same, when the talking points are the same. And the lawyer's points are the same, then we start to see that this is not an organic local movement."
THE HIDDEN LEFT-WING NETWORK POWERING A ‘CONSERVATIVE’ REBELLION AGAINST A MAJOR TRUMP PRIORITY

Volunteers hand out yard signs against a data center complex in Canaan Valley on June 30, 2025, after a public meeting organized by the West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection regarding an air quality permit application for a gas-fired power plant near Davis, W. Va. (ULYSSE BELLIER/AFP via Getty Images)

The main driver of left-wing groups opposing data centers, in addition to ideological disdain toward President Donald Trump, who has been a staunch supporter of American AI dominance, is the opposition to fossil fuels, Behrens says.

"It's the same thing that they've always opposed, any real progress they're going to be against, anything that strengthens America, they're gonna be against, and when it comes to data centers, the reason they're against them is absolutely clear because it represents American jobs, and it has to be supported by American energy," Behrens explained.

"And those are two things that the environmental left just absolutely cannot stand. And they're gonna use delay or distracting tactics. They're gonna use tactics like saying it's about the water, it's about land use. But lo and behold, when it comes time to grow cannabis, they're more than happy with the water use. When it comes time to plaster solar fields across farmland, they don't care about land use. When it comes time to put their solar fields across an endangered species area, they don't care about that endangered species. It's never what they say it's about, it's always against progress and production for American energy and American workers really."

Data centers have become one of the most talked about political issues of the midterm election season, particularly in states like Texas, Ohio and Nevada, and Fox News polling this summer found voters overwhelmingly oppose building data centers in their own communities, with 70% opposed and 30% in favor.
AGITATORS UNITED BY CHINESE MONEY, HATE FOR AMERICA TARGET DATA CENTERS, EXPERTS WARN
George Soros pictured on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in January 2020. (Simon Dawson/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Nearly 8 in 10 voters said construction should move more slowly to address environmental and local concerns, while just 20% favored building as quickly as possible to preserve the U.S. competitive edge over China and other countries. Opposition crossed generational lines, though MAGA Republicans and Republican men were the most supportive groups, at 46% and 45%, respectively.

In a recent Fox News Digital op-ed, Consumers’ Research Executive Director Will Hild made the case that data center developers ignoring the concerns of the consumers’ has been a problem that could cost the United States victory in the AI race.

"Climate radicals who spent decades trying to kill fracking, pipelines, and American energy dominance have found their next target," Hild told Fox News Digital. "They are hijacking legitimate consumer concerns to fuel a massive disinformation campaign aimed at frightening Americans into shutting down the technology infrastructure. The same activist machine that fought American oil and gas is now mobilizing against modern data centers, because its answer to American innovation is always to stop building begins."

Data center backlash is increasingly reshaping midterm races nationwide, with candidates in both parties facing pressure to distance themselves from data center development or demand tougher restrictions as voters raise concerns about electricity costs, water use and the impact on local communities.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The issue has emerged in major Senate and gubernatorial contests from Ohio and Michigan to Pennsylvania and Texas, with campaigns using data centers in attack ads and candidates who once touted the projects increasingly calling for new regulations, tax changes or construction pauses.

In Texas, the fight has also become part of Democrats’ broader midterm organizing effort in the state. Texas Together, a $30 million coordinated campaign backed by the Texas Democratic Party, Texas Majority PAC, Beto O’Rourke’s Powered by People and other Democratic groups, has hosted data center-focused town halls and press events featuring Democratic candidates, while the El Paso Young Democrats and El Paso County Democratic Party organized a protest against what they called "destructive AI Data Centers."
Behrens agreed with Hild’s call for different messaging and spoke to Fox News Digital about what data center companies need to do to shift the narrative.

"I think they need to discuss very specifically with local stakeholders, not the ones that are being astroturfed in, they need to talk about the benefits of it, they need to talk about exactly what the data center does because there are legitimate questions about it and Americans have a right to say, what is this going up in our area?"

Behrens added, "But I would also caution to say if you're not throwing up opposition to any other type of manufacturing, if you're not throwing up opposition to a large Buc-ees gas station then why the anger over data centers? Because those operations can use a lot of water, they can use a lot of land just like the data centers. So asking the questions is absolutely legitimate, but throwing up needless roadblocks because this is something that the environmental left has told you to dislike, we really need to watch out for that. And I think the bottom line would be if AOC, Bernie Sanders and Kathy Hochul are your intellectual guiding stars for opposing data centers, then you need to really think about where you stand because they've been wrong on every major energy issue ever since they entered public office."
Fox News Digital reached out to CodePink, the Sierra Club, Open Society Foundations and Public Citizen for comment.
In a statement to Fox News Digital, a Sixteen Thirty Fund spokesperson pushed back saying the group "proudly supported the Sierra Club."

The spokesperson added: "Across the country, people have legitimate questions about how these projects could affect their communities. Dismissing those concerns as anti-American or anti-progress is absurd. Corporate interests should focus on addressing the potential impacts of data center development rather than attacking those who speak out."
Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter at Fox News. Find him on Twitter @andymarkmiller and email tips to AndrewMark.Miller@Fox.com.

title: Hasan Piker cheerleads progressives as 80-year-old senator wins six more years
summary: Hasan Piker celebrated Ed Markey's Massachusetts primary win over Seth Moulton, calling it proof that progressive policies and trans rights are winning.
story: Incumbent Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., and Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., faced off over transgender athletes, ICE, socialism and term limits in their final debate before the Sept. 1 Democratic primary. (Credit: WCVB)

Hasan Piker, a controversial Twitch streamer and far-left activist who has supported several challengers against moderate Democrats, celebrated the victory of Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., in a primary contest that pitted the 80-year-old progressive stalwart against a far younger and more centrist candidate.

"It’s very clear that the Dem voters care more about policies and having a progressive represent them in the Senate than age! Another w for our movement!" Piker wrote on X after Markey defeated Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., who is 33 years his junior.

Markey defeated Moulton, who centered his campaign on generational change, by casting himself as the race's true progressive. He repeatedly questioned Moulton's progressive credentials while continuing to push for transgender rights, particularly in sports — a position many Democrats have shied away from.
DEMOCRATS’ GENERATIONAL BATTLE ERUPTS AS 80-YEAR-OLD SENATOR FACES YOUNGER CHALLENGER
Former Democrat operative Evan Barker says the party needs to realize that controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker is quickly becoming the face of their movement. (Julia Demaree/AP Photo)

The position, which Republicans have used as a political rallying cry on the campaign trail and which Democrats have largely avoided as they push to flip both chambers of Congress, is one that Moulton argued played a major role in Democrats' losses across the board in 2024.
"Trans athletes should be able to play," Markey told The New York Times. "That reflects Massachusetts and who we are. And Seth Moulton does not."
Markey has also supported aggressive legislation on climate change, a platform that helped win over even groups that center around younger audiences.

"VICTORY! Congratulations to Ed Markey on his victory in Massachusetts tonight. Sen. Markey has been a leading climate champion in the fight for a Green New Deal to create jobs and lower costs for working people," the Sunrise Movement said in a statement to X.
HOUSE PROGRESSIVES REVIVE GREEN NEW DEAL FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS AS DEM CIVIL WAR EMPOWERS FAR LEFT
Sen. Ed Markey, the more progressive of the two candidates, has the backing of Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Ayanna Pressley. (Jemal Countess/Getty Images for MoveOn Civic Action)
The group describes itself as a "movement of young people fighting fascism to win a Green New Deal."

David Axelrod, a top political consultant and former advisor to President Barack Obama, noted that Markey hadn’t always been a darling of the progressive left ahead of Tuesday’s election. He credited Markey’s pivot for his political longevity.
"[Ed Markey] was first elected to Congress 50 yrs ago as a social conservative, opposed to abortion rights and school busing," Axelrod said in his own post to X.

"Now 80, he's likely to sail in tonight's primary in MA, despite his age, because, in his Golden Years, he's grabbed on to the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, trans rights and other marquee priorities of the Left, undergirding himself against younger, more moderate challengers in very blue MA."
Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., also praised Markey's win. Like Markey, Sanders, 84, continues to shape the progressive movement despite the decades between him and many of its younger candidates.

"Congratulations to Ed Markey on his landslide victory in the Democratic Massachusetts Senate primary. Ed knows that, at a time of massive income and wealth inequality, Congress must take on the billionaires and fight for working families," Sanders wrote.
AOC ENDORSES SEN ED MARKEY AS INCUMBENT FACES DEM US SENATE PRIMARY CHALLENGE FROM REP SETH MOULTON

U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) hugs Sen. Ed Markey (D-MA) as they speak at a news conference on the launch of the American Climate Corps outside the U.S. Capitol building on September 20, 2023, in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)
Having cleared the primary election, Markey now heads to the general election on Nov. 3, when he is heavily favored to win in the deep-blue Bay State.

Markey last won re-election in a 66.2% to 33.0% victory over Republican challenger Kevin O’Connor, a local attorney.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: Progressive push hits wall against conservative Democrat in deep-blue district
summary: Stephen Lynch defeated progressive challenger Patrick Roath in the Massachusetts 8th Congressional District Democratic primary despite clashes over ICE.
story: Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., criticized his party for lacking a clear immigration plan, relying on opposition to President Donald Trump and downplaying inflation under former President Joe Biden.
Rep. Stephen Lynch, who has cultivated a relatively conservative reputation while representing Massachusetts for the past quarter-century, has defeated a well-funded progressive challenger.

Patrick Roath, an attorney and one-time aide for former Massachusetts Gov. Deval Patrick, challenged Lynch from the left, outraising him by about $300,000. Lynch and Roath clashed over a number of issues on the campaign trail, namely immigration, healthcare, money in politics and housing.

Lynch was one of 46 House Democrats to vote in favor of the Laken Riley Act, legislation requiring federal authorities to detain certain migrants accused or convicted of theft and other specified crimes. Roath, who supported dismantling and replacing ICE, cited Lynch’s support for the bill as part of his reason for entering the race.
MEET THE FAR-LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT IN 2026 MIDTERMS
Rep. Stephen Lynch speaks with reporters during a news conference on August 4, 2019, in South Boston, Massachusetts. (Staff Photo By Angela Rowlings/MediaNews Group/Boston Herald)

Roath criticized Lynch’s support of the bill as "shortsighted and expedient" and argued that it "demonstrates a fundamental failure to take seriously the threat that the Trump Administration poses to all Americans."
Lynch acknowledged that the Laken Riley Act was "imperfect" but defended his vote principally as a response to what he called an immigration system that was "completely out of control."

On healthcare, Roath supported moving toward universal, government-funded coverage and has backed Medicare for All, while Lynch has supported a public option and sharply criticized the role of for-profit companies in the hospital system.

Lynch, notably, was one of just a handful of Democrats to vote against the Affordable Care Act. The congressman justified his vote by arguing that it provided too many concessions to insurance companies.
AOC SAYS MAHA ADVOCATES' FIGHT 'ISN'T PARTISAN' AS SHE BLASTS HEALTHCARE SYSTEM FOR FUELING 'A TON OF ANXIETY'

A House Weaponization Committee hearing went off the rails Thursday as Democrat Rep. Stephen Lynch, D-Mass., shouted at Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, over his party's ability to "cross-examine" testimony provided by prominent Republicans. (Tom Williams, Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

While Roath ran as an outsider populist, Lynch attempted to challenge that posturing by pointing to the progressive’s career as a corporate lawyer. Before becoming a member of Congress in 2001, Lynch was previously an ironworker, union president and lawyer.
Both Lynch and Roath managed to pull together an impressive coalition of supporters.

The Boston Globe, David Hogg’s Leaders We Deserve, Indivisible, Massachusetts Teachers Association, Boston Teachers Union and American Federation of Teachers Massachusetts all endorsed Roath, while Lynch secured the backing of the Massachusetts AFL-CIO, Iron Workers Local 7, Professional Firefighters of Massachusetts and the American Federation of Government Employees.

In addition to falling within the context of the power struggle between the Democratic Party’s progressive and moderate wings, the primary in Massachusetts’s 8th Congressional District was also a generational battle. Lynch is 71 and Roath is just 39.

Rep. Stephen Lynch, D-Mass., arrives for a meeting of the House Democratic Caucus and President Joe Biden on the infrastructure bill in the U.S. Capitol on Friday, October 1, 2021. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
'EXTREMIST' AND 'BARBARIC': MASSACHUSETTS DEMOCRATS BREAK RANKS OVER NEW ABORTION LAW
Despite his voting record, Lynch has said that his reputation as a conservative or a moderate is overstated.
"Calling me the least liberal member from Massachusetts is like calling me the slowest Kenyan in the Boston Marathon," he said in 2010. "It's all relative."

While Lynch is conservative compared to his colleagues in the Massachusetts delegation, he has shifted to the left in recent years. Once a proud pro-life Democrat, the long-time congressman now defends Planned Parenthood and throws his support behind pro-abortion legislation.

Massachusetts' 8th Congressional District is heavily Democratic. Robert Burke, a retired telecommunications worker and small businessman, is the GOP’s nominee in the constituency.

title: One of Congress' most powerful Democrats just survived a progressive primary revolt
summary: Richard Neal defeated progressive challenger Jeromie Whalen in the Massachusetts 1st Congressional District primary, but the seniority debate rages on.
story: Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram reports from Capitol Hill on House Republicans forcing floor votes for Democrats to disavow socialism. The legislative strategy follows statements from former Obama White House Chief of Staff Rahm Emanuel and New Hampshire Senate candidate Chris Pappas distancing themselves from Democratic socialists.

The progressive push to unseat a veteran Democratic power broker fell short Tuesday, when Rep. Richard Neal defeated high school teacher Jeromie Whalen in Massachusetts' 1st Congressional District primary.

Neal, 77, has represented western Massachusetts in Congress for nearly four decades and has built considerable influence as the top Democrat on the powerful tax-writing House Ways and Means Committee. His 39-year-old challenger ran on a platform that included Medicare for All, higher taxes on the wealthy, abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement and a pledge to reject campaign contributions from corporate PACs.
The race tested whether progressive voters were ready to replace a longtime Democratic incumbent, even if it meant giving up the clout Neal’s seniority brings western Massachusetts.
2026 MIDTERMS: PRIMARIES, KEY RACES AND ELECTION RESULTS

A 39-year-old public-school teacher tried to unseat one of the House’s most powerful Democrats. On Tuesday, Rep. Richard Neal prevailed, preserving the veteran lawmaker’s hold on a key western Massachusetts seat. (Al Drago/Bloomberg/Getty Images)

Whalen sought to cast Neal as a representative of the Democratic establishment unwilling to take on wealthy interests and corporate power, while pitching himself as part of a younger generation pushing the party further to the left.

Neal, meanwhile, made his experience and position in Washington central to his case for re-election, arguing that his seniority gives the district influence in Congress that would be difficult for a first-term lawmaker to replicate.

The contest also unfolded against a broader debate inside the Democratic Party over its aging leadership and whether longtime incumbents should step aside for a younger generation. Progressive stalwart Sen. Ed Markey, 80, defeated a more moderate challenger 33 years his junior on Tuesday night.
MEET THE FAR-LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT IN 2026

Considered the "Dean" of the Massachusetts House delegation, the 77-year-old Democrat is once again seeking re-election, hoping to close in on almost 40 years of representing western Massachusetts in Washington. (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
Neal's position on the Ways and Means Committee also gave the race significance beyond western Massachusetts.

The panel sits at the center of congressional fights over taxes and other major economic policy. His victory also ultimately preserves the seat of one of the House Democratic caucus' most senior members while turning back a challenge built around the argument that the party needs generational and ideological change.

The race became a choice between replacing a longtime Democratic incumbent with a new progressive upstart. (Joseph Prezioso/AFP/Getty Images)
There is no Republican filed to run against Neal in the general election.

title: Biden-Harris favorite gets second shot at Congress, beats Squad-backed candidate
summary: Dan Koh, backed by Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, won a crowded Democratic primary for the House seat Seth Moulton is vacating in Massachusetts.
story: Incumbent Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., and Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., faced off over transgender athletes, ICE, socialism and term limits in their final debate before the Sept. 1 Democratic primary. (Credit: WCVB)
A former Biden administration aide just won a crowded primary race in Massachusetts, setting up a glide path to the House of Representatives come November.

Dan Koh came out first among six candidates to replace Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., who ended his House tenure with a failed run for Senate against incumbent Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., that came to a conclusion Tuesday night.

Koh had the backing of both former President Joe Biden and former Vice President Kamala Harris, which was no surprise after his stint working in the White House. He first joined the administration as chief of staff to then-Labor Secretary Marty Walsh and later became deputy assistant to the president and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs.
BIDEN INTERVENES IN DEM CONGRESSIONAL PRIMARY, WARNING ALL 'WE DID TO HELP ORDINARY PEOPLE IS IN JEOPARDY NOW'

Congressional candidate Dan Koh participates in a debate between the Democratic candidates for the 3rd Congressional District seat in Lowell, Mass., on April 29, 2018. (Keith Bedford/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

But his successful Tuesday primary is not the first time Koh ran for Congress. He narrowly lost the Democratic nomination in Massachusetts' nearby 3rd Congressional District to Rep. Lori Trahan, D-Mass., in 2018.
Koh is running on progressive campaign promises like abolishing "Trump's ICE," referring to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and universal healthcare.
He's now poised to succeed Moulton in the 6th Congressional District, which includes the northeastern portion of Massachusetts and is rated a safe blue seat.
HARRIS-BACKED DEMOCRAT SCRUBS BLM-ERA POSTS AS HOUSE CAMPAIGN HEATS UP
Moulton, who served in the Marine Corps, has represented the district since 2015.
Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Seth Moulton stand at lecterns ahead of their debate at WWLP-22News on July 8, 2026. (Suzanne Kreiter/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
His campaign for Senate has been marked by a bitter primary battle against Markey, an 80-year-old progressive who has been in office since 2013.

Moulton, 47, ran his campaign based on generational change and arguing that Markey had long missed his chance to substantively make life better for Massachusetts residents, but that wasn't enough to stave him off Tuesday.
AOC ENDORSES SEN ED MARKEY AS INCUMBENT FACES DEM US SENATE PRIMARY CHALLENGE FROM REP SETH MOULTON

Markey is backed by the far left's marquee names, including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt. Meanwhile, Koh himself is a figure of the establishment left, with both his father and uncle also serving in the federal government.
Former President Joe Biden speaks during the opening of the Barack Obama Presidential Center in Chicago. (Kent Nishimura/AFP via Getty Images)

His father, Howard Koh, was an assistant secretary in the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) under former President Barack Obama. His uncle served under the Obama and Clinton administrations.

Koh now moves on to face Republican military veteran Micah Jones, who is running in his primary unopposed.

title: Top Democrat survives double-barreled challenge as party’s Israel divide hits home
summary: House Minority Whip Katherine Clark advanced past two left-wing challengers who made Gaza and AIPAC money central issues in the Democratic primary.
story: Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., weighs in on the Democratic Party’s internal debate over U.S. aid to Israel and more during ‘The Sunday Briefing.’

House Democratic Whip Katherine Clark toppled two progressive challengers Tuesday in Massachusetts' safely Democratic 5th Congressional District, surviving a primary fight that put Gaza and pro-Israel political spending at the center of the race.

Clark, who won handily Tuesday night against fellow Democratic Party contenders Jonathan Paz and Tarik Samman, was first elected in 2013 during a special election and has held her position as House Democratic whip since 2022.

The second-highest ranking Democrat after House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Clark has helped lead opposition to Republican spending, immigration and healthcare measures, including recent messaging against ICE funding and GOP cuts to Head Start and Medicaid.
MEET THE FAR-LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT IN 2026 MIDTERMS

U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark, D-Mass., arrives for a leadership election meeting with the Democratic caucus in the Longworth House Office Building on Capitol Hill Nov. 30, 2022 in Washington, D.C. Clark is running for the No. 2 position in House Democratic leadership aft4er the departure of Rep. Steny Hoyer, D-Md., from the leadership group. (Drew Angerer/Getty Images)
She ran against former city councilor, educator and union organizer Paz and 27-year-old Harvard Law School researcher and union organizer Samman.
Clark fended off two left-wing challengers who sought to make Gaza and pro-Israel political money central issues in the safely blue Boston-area primary.
Her fundraising operation dwarfed both challengers, raising $4.5 million, while Paz raised $88,500 and Samman brought in $43,800, according to FEC filings.
PELOSI-BACKED DEMOCRAT LOSES AFTER $10M FLOOD OF CRYPTO, PRO-ISRAEL MONEY

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., right, joined at center-left by Rep. Katherine Clark, D-Mass., the House minority whip, rallies Democrats against the Republican budget plan on the House steps at the Capitol in Washington Feb. 25. (AP/J. Scott Applewhite)

While AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, endorsed Clark and has contributed to her campaign in the past, she has taken a critical stance toward the Israeli government’s handling of the war in Gaza.
AIPAC is an influential pro-Israel lobbying group that has been criticized for advocating for U.S. military aid to Israel amid the war in Gaza.

Last year, Clark used the word "genocide" at a district event before clarifying that she was not accusing Israel of genocide. Then, in July, she voted to cut $3.3 billion in U.S. military aid, saying Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government had failed to meet U.S. interests and values.
Clark has continued to support Israel as a sovereign Jewish state and backed U.S. assistance for some Israeli defensive systems but is critical of Netanyahu.
TOP HOUSE DEMOCRAT SAYS ANTI-ISRAEL ACTIVISTS’ THREATS KEPT HIM FROM TOWN HALLS FOR A YEAR
U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark, D-Mass., speaks during a news conference on protecting women's reproductive health care July 28, 2022, on Capitol Hill in Washington. (AP Photo/Mariam Zuhaib, File)
Samman and Paz have argued that while Clark has increasingly criticized Israel’s conduct in Gaza, she has yet to renounce the AIPAC money she has accepted.

title: House Democrat survives left-flank challenge as Bernie volunteer mounts insurgent bid
summary: Jake Auchincloss advanced against progressive challenger Jason Poulos, who campaigned on Medicare-for-all and ending U.S. military aid to Israel.
story: Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., asserts that an official anti-Israel stance by the Democratic Party would be his 'red line,' potentially leading him to leave the party. A recent House vote saw 103 Democrats block aid to Israel, signaling a major shift.
Rep. Jake Auchincloss advanced Tuesday against Jason Poulos in Massachusetts’ 4th Congressional District.
Auchincloss has held his seat since 2021 and faced his first Democratic primary challenge since winning the seat.

Progressive challenger Poulos is an AI policy researcher who has been critical of Auchincloss regarding past support for military aid to Israel and ties to AIPAC while calling for an end to U.S. military assistance to Israel.
PROGRESSIVE WAVE CRASHES IN SUN BELT BATTLEGROUND AS MODERATE HOLDS HIS SEAT
Rep. Jake Auchincloss, D-Mass., speaks during the House Democrats' news conference on the Republican economic agenda in the Capitol April 9, 2025. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Poulos, who previously volunteered for Bernie Sanders’ campaign, ran on Medicare-for-all, universal basic income, taxes on corporate automation, stronger unions and student debt cancellation. He also wanted to reduce military spending and end U.S. military aid to Israel.

While Auchincloss is endorsed by AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, he has been critical of aspects of Israel's conduct in Gaza by saying some Israeli actions in 2025 "crossed lines" on humanitarian conditions.
AIPAC is an influential pro-Israel lobbying group that has been criticized for advocating for U.S. military aid to Israel amid the war in Gaza.
HOUSE DEMOCRATS FRACTURE BADLY OVER MASSIE AMENDMENT TO CUT $3.3B IN U.S. AID TO ISRAEL

President Donald Trump hosts Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at Mar-a-Lago Dec. 29, 2025, with talks addressing Iran’s renewed threats and potential progress on the next phase of the Gaza peace framework. (Israel Government Press Office)
In July, Auchincloss voted with more than 100 House Democrats to eliminate $3.3 billion in U.S. military financing for Israel, while maintaining his support for the U.S.-Israel alliance.
Auchincloss campaigned on lowering housing and healthcare costs, promoting economic growth and positioning Democrats to better confront the economic disruption caused by AI.

The Pentagon in Arlington, Va., Oct. 22, 2025. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
Auchincloss, who succeeded Joe Kennedy III, comes from a prominent Boston medical family.
He had previously been a registered Republican and worked on former Gov. Charlie Baker’s campaign, a line his primary opponents used against him. He later returned to the Democratic Party.

title: Trump taps ‘true warrior’ Hung Cao as Navy secretary after 4 months as acting leader
summary: Hung Cao, a retired Navy captain and special operations veteran, has led the Department of the Navy for four months as President Trump now seeks Senate confirmation.
story: Acting U.S. Navy Secretary Hung Cao discusses U.S. military assets in the Middle East and Iran's strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’

President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that he is nominating acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao to permanently lead the service, calling the former Navy special operations officer a "true WARRIOR" and urging the Senate to quickly confirm him.

Cao has served as acting secretary for the past four months, overseeing the Navy and Marine Corps as the Trump administration pushes to expand U.S. shipbuilding and strengthen the military’s maritime capabilities.
"I am pleased to nominate a true WARRIOR, Hung Cao, to become the next Secretary of the Navy," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"We need Patriots like Hung leading our Navy and Marine Corps, and I can think of no one better than him to make sure our Great Navy and Marine Corps remain the FIERCEST and BEST Force the World has ever seen," the president continued.
TRUMP PRAISES OUSTED NAVY SECRETARY PHELAN AMID TENSIONS WITH PENTAGON LEADERSHIP

Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao testifies during the Senate Armed Services Committee hearing titled "The Posture of the Department of the Navy in review of the Defense Authorization Request for FY2027 and the Future Years Defense Program," in the Dirksen building on Tuesday, May 19, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
Trump called on the Senate to move quickly on the nomination, pointing to Cao’s tenure already leading the department.
SENATE REPUBLICANS CONFIRM NEARLY 50 OF TRUMP'S PICKS FOR ENERGY, LAND MANAGEMENT
"The Senate needs to confirm this Warfighter, ASAP, so he can continue the fantastic work he has been doing over the past 4 months," Trump wrote.
Cao thanked Trump shortly after the announcement and said his priorities would continue to include shipbuilding and homeland defense.
AS CHINA TENSIONS LOOM, US TEMPORARILY PAUSES TAIWAN WEAPONS SALES DUE TO IRAN WAR, ACTING NAVY SECRETARY SAYS

President Trump praised Hung Cao as a "true WARRIOR" and urged the Senate to quickly confirm him as Navy secretary, saying Cao is the best person to lead the Navy and Marine Corps and strengthen shipbuilding and homeland defense. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

"Thank you, Mr. President. It’s an honor of a lifetime to lead the great warriors of the Navy and Marine Corps team," Cao wrote on X. "I’m grateful for your leadership and support as we continue to get after shipbuilding and ensure the defense of the homeland."

Cao is a retired Navy captain who served for 25 years in uniform after graduating from the U.S. Naval Academy. His military career included service in special operations and deployments to combat zones, including Iraq and Afghanistan.
The Virginia Republican later entered politics, mounting an unsuccessful bid for Congress in 2022 before challenging Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine for his Senate seat in 2024.

Trump endorsed Cao during the 2024 campaign, touting his military background. Cao ultimately lost to Kaine before joining the Trump administration and taking over the Navy in an acting capacity earlier this year.
TRUMP TAPS ACTING LABOR SECRETARY KEITH SONDERLING FOR PERMANENT ROLE PENDING SENATE CONFIRMATION
Under Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao acknowledged the impact of the COVID-19 vaccine mandate on service members dismissed from the military. (U.S. Navy)
If confirmed by the Senate, Cao would formally assume responsibility for the Department of the Navy, which includes both the Navy and Marine Corps.

title: Self-funded CEO claims GOP nomination to challenge Massachusetts Democrat’s second-term bid
summary: Mike Minogue won 70% at the Massachusetts GOP convention and defeated former MBTA executive Brian Shortsleeve to take on Gov. Maura Healey.
story: On the eve of the state GOP convention, former Abiomed CEO and Desert Storm veteran Mike Minogue pledges to bring common-sense problem-solving skills to the Bay State as he takes on Maura Healey.
Former medical device executive Mike Minogue won the Massachusetts gubernatorial primary Tuesday, defeating Brian Shortsleeve, a former executive at the MBTA, the state-run transit agency.

The winner will now face favored Democratic Gov. Maura Healey, who is running for a second term. Massachusetts has had continuous Democratic representation in Congress since 1996, but Republicans have had considerably more success in races for the governor's mansion since the Reagan era.
Minogue emphasized his business credentials in campaign materials, citing his work at GE Healthcare before leading Danvers-based Abiomed.
GOP GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE FIGHTING TO FLIP BLUE STATE UNVEILS HEALTHCARE PLAN TO LOWER COSTS, EXPAND ACCESS
Combat veteran-turned-CEO Mike Minogue launched a Republican campaign for governor in Massachusetts (Mike Minogue campaign)
Minogue said that, while he was at Abiomed, the company developed the world’s smallest heart pump and doubled the size of its headquarters, increasing its in-state capabilities and creating jobs.

Minogue also drew attention on social media when Boston-based Canadian American investor Kevin O’Leary, better known as Shark Tank’s "Mr. Wonderful," appeared in one of his videos and said he does not usually "show for politicians."
"Massachusetts is ‘dead-money’ now. We need a guy like this to run the show," O’Leary said in July.
TRUMP KEEPS WINNING REPUBLICAN PRIMARIES; HIS LOSSES MAY BE MORE REVEALING
The Boston skyline (Getty Images)
According to The Boston Herald, Healey launched a last-minute ad attacking Minogue as "MAGA Mike," which the newspaper said shows the executive "has Healey’s attention" and may help Shortsleeve.

Minogue won the state’s GOP convention endorsement with 70% of the vote, while Shortsleeve earned his ballot position with a fraction of a percentage point more than the required 15%, according to reports.

Minogue self-funded roughly $7 million of the more than $7.5 million he raised in the first quarter, hosted a fundraiser with Vice President JD Vance and has donated to Trump and the RNC. Shortsleeve raised about $646,500 in the first quarter of 2026.
Healey was formally renominated Tuesday after running unopposed. Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll, a fellow Democrat, also advances unopposed to the November election.

Republicans, however, have no candidates in about half of the state’s congressional districts or in the races for secretary of state and state auditor. A signature problem has forced lieutenant gubernatorial candidate Anne Manning Martin to run a write-in campaign.

The district in the Berkshires, the district covering much of the Massachusetts Turnpike corridor, and two exurban Boston-area districts to the north and west have no Republican candidates competing Tuesday, guaranteeing Democratic nominees will advance in those races ahead of November.
Massachusetts state government has not always been as reliably Democratic in modern times despite the conditions in this year’s contests.
Former Gov. Charlie Baker, a moderate Republican, preceded Healey from 2015 to 2023.
Former Sen. Mitt Romney, R-Utah, served as Massachusetts governor from 2003 to 2007 and opted against re-election before launching an unsuccessful presidential bid against President Barack Obama.

title: Cybercrime losses near $21B: 5 ways to protect your money
summary: The FBI reports nearly $21 billion in cybercrime losses for 2025, up 26%, as AI scams make fake voices and identities more convincing than ever.
story: Cybercrime losses reached nearly $21 billion last year, prompting Kurt Knutsson to warn of increasingly sophisticated AI scams. He joins 'Fox & Friends Weekend' to break down the FBI data, highlighting that investment fraud alone cost victims $8.65 billion. Knutsson hosts a free live class to teach families how to protect their money and secure accounts.

Nearly $21 billion. That number jumped out at me when I looked at the FBI's latest cybercrime data. Behind that enormous loss are families who watched savings disappear and people who trusted the wrong investment pitch. Some victims had no clue someone was moving their money until they checked an account.

Americans reported nearly $21 billion in losses to cyber-enabled crime during 2025, up 26% from the year before. Investment fraud caused the biggest financial hit at about $8.65 billion. I recently joined "Fox & Friends Weekend" to talk about those numbers and a bigger problem I see coming. Scammers now have AI tools that can make a fake message, voice or identity far more believable than the clumsy scams many of us learned to recognize years ago. That changes how we need to protect our money.
Here are five practical steps you can take now to put stronger barriers between scammers and your savings.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.
Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com
IDENTITY THEFT LOSSES SURGE 70% FOR OLDER AMERICANS

Americans reported nearly $21 billion in cyber-enabled crime losses in 2025, as scammers increasingly used artificial intelligence to make fraud more convincing. (Hollie Adams/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
AI is helping scammers sound more convincing

For years, one of the standard pieces of scam advice was to look for obvious mistakes. Maybe an email had terrible grammar. Perhaps the caller sounded suspicious. AI can now erase many of those clues.

The FBI says its Internet Crime Complaint Center received 22,364 complaints in 2025 that included AI-related information. Reported losses tied to those complaints reached about $893 million. The FBI also warns that criminals can use AI to create fake social profiles, cloned voices and convincing videos.

That gives scammers another way to build trust before asking for money or personal information. So telling you to "be careful" no longer feels like enough advice to me. I want barriers between a scammer and your money.
5 ways to protect your money from cybercrime
You cannot predict every scam that may come your way. However, you can put safeguards in place that make it harder for a criminal to reach your money.

Start with your bank and credit cards. Open the official app or website for each financial institution and look for notification settings. Turn on alerts for transactions and transfers. You may also be able to receive warnings about suspicious account activity.

The exact choices vary by bank. However, the goal stays simple. If money moves and you did not authorize it, you want to know quickly. I have talked with victims who discovered fraud long after criminals gained access. A real-time alert gives you a chance to call the financial institution and react much sooner.

Next, check the security settings on your bank, credit card and investment accounts. Use a strong password that you do not reuse elsewhere, which a password manager can help you create and store. Then turn on two-factor or multifactor authentication (2FA) wherever your financial institution offers it.

If the company supports an authenticator app, passkey or another stronger verification method, consider using that option. Texted security codes still add protection, although your phone number can become a target in a SIM swap attack.

Also protect the email account connected to your finances. A criminal who controls your email may be able to reset passwords or intercept account notifications. For a closer look at the different login options, see Are bank text codes enough to protect you?

Your phone number has quietly become part of your financial security. In a SIM swap or port-out scam, a criminal tricks a carrier into moving your number to another SIM or device. Once that happens, calls and texted security codes can start going to the scammer.

Contact your carrier or check its account-security settings. Look for a number transfer lock, port-out protection or another feature designed to block unauthorized transfers. If your phone suddenly loses service for no clear reason, pay attention. Contact your carrier from another device, especially if you also notice unusual activity involving your financial accounts.
IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT
Investment fraud accounted for about $8.65 billion in reported losses as cybercrime cost Americans nearly $21 billion in 2025. (Bildquelle/ullstein bild via Getty Images)

A credit freeze remains one of the strongest free tools available for preventing new-account fraud. You need to place a freeze separately with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. Once active, the freeze restricts access to your credit file and makes it much harder for someone to open a new credit account using your identity.

A freeze does not hurt your credit score. You can also lift it when you legitimately need to apply for credit. One warning: go directly to the official credit bureau websites rather than clicking an ad or unfamiliar search result. Criminals know people search for credit-freeze help too. CyberGuy has step-by-step guidance on how to freeze your credit and clean up your online data at Cyberguy.com

This one worries me because retirement accounts can represent decades of someone's work. We recently covered a case involving a Colgate-Palmolive employee whose entire $751,430 401(k) was allegedly drained after an impostor changed the account's contact information. The case later settled on undisclosed terms.

Log in to your retirement and investment accounts and review their security settings. Make sure your contact information remains correct. Turn on account alerts and multifactor authentication. Then ask your brokerage or retirement-plan provider what protections it offers for withdrawals and transfers. Some providers offer additional verification or other controls that can make unauthorized transfers harder. This deserves the same attention you give your checking account. Maybe more.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay

If you want to go deeper than the steps above, I will walk through each one in more detail in my CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today's Biggest Threats . The live event has ended, but the full replay and CyberGuy Money Protection checklist are available now.

In the class, I show you how to put these protections in place step by step, including where to look for bank alerts, how to strengthen account logins, ways to lock down your phone number, how to freeze your credit and what to ask your retirement or investment provider about added safeguards. You can pause the replay and work through each step at your own pace.
Watch the free CyberGuy LIVE replay and get the Money Protection checklist at CyberGuyLive.com
YOUR BANK MAY STOP TEXTING YOU SIX-DIGIT CODES
Artificial intelligence can help scammers create convincing messages, cloned voices, fake identities and videos designed to gain victims’ trust. (Nikos Pekiaridis/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Kurt's key takeaways

What worries me about the FBI's nearly $21 billion figure goes beyond the size of the number. Scammers have become better at taking advantage of moments when people naturally trust what they see or hear. AI raises the stakes because a familiar voice or polished message can create a false sense of confidence. The FBI's numbers show how much money is already disappearing through cyber-enabled crime. I would rather see you build protections now than depend on spotting one tiny clue in the middle of a convincing scam. Turn on the alerts and secure the accounts holding your money. Then look at the protections surrounding your phone number, credit and retirement savings. Cybercriminals only need one good opportunity. Your job is to make that opportunity much harder to find.

title: Uber lets parents watch teen rides live
summary: Uber teen accounts now feature live video streaming from the driver's camera, but encrypted recordings stay on Uber's servers for up to 14 days.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
School, soccer practice, a shift at work or a friend's house. Teens have places to go, and parents can't always be there for every ride. Uber is giving families a new way to check in.

The company is adding live video streaming to Uber Teen Accounts, allowing a linked parent or guardian to see their teen inside the vehicle during an active ride. The feed comes from the front-facing camera on the driver's smartphone.
Uber says the feature is live now in nine U.S. markets. Uber plans a nationwide rollout over the coming weeks.

If you have a teen who uses Uber, the idea may sound reassuring. However, a live camera inside the car also raises privacy questions. Who can watch? Does Uber see the stream? What happens to the video after the ride? Uber gave CyberGuy more detail on exactly how the feature works.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today's Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.
Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com
HOUSTON UBER DRIVER CAUGHT IN WILD POLICE CHASE AS OFFICERS SEEN ON DASHCAM VIDEO HITCHING A RIDE IN HIS CAR
Uber is adding live video to Teen Accounts, allowing linked parents or guardians to check on teens during active rides. (Klaudia Radecka/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
How Uber Teen Accounts live video works

Uber launched Teen Accounts in 2023 to give teenagers more independence while keeping their rides connected to a parent or guardian. Now, live video adds another option for families who want more visibility during a trip.

If a driver has live video enabled, Uber sends a push notification to the parent or guardian linked to the teen's account when the ride begins. The parent can tap the notification and watch the live feed through the driver's front-facing smartphone camera.

Uber says both the teen and the driver receive a notification when the parent begins watching. Everyone inside the vehicle knows when the livestream is active. Only the parent or guardian linked to the teen's account can view the live video during the trip, according to Uber. Uber also told CyberGuy that the company cannot access the live video in real time.
Where Uber teen live video is available
The feature is starting in a limited number of U.S. markets before expanding more broadly.
Uber told CyberGuy that live video is currently available in:
AtlantaPhoenixOrlandoRaleigh-DurhamPortland, OregonSan AntonioClevelandRhode IslandEl Paso
Atlanta
Phoenix
Orlando
Raleigh-Durham
Portland, Oregon
San Antonio
Cleveland
Rhode Island
El Paso
Uber says it will roll out live video nationwide over the coming weeks. Keep in mind that availability also depends on whether the driver has live video enabled.
What happens to the video after an Uber ride?

This is the privacy detail parents should know before using the feature. Uber says the live video is encrypted. After the trip, the driver cannot access the recording. The teen cannot access it either. The linked parent or guardian also loses access once the ride ends.

However, the encrypted recording does remain on Uber's servers for a period of time. Uber told CyberGuy that the encrypted video recording is automatically deleted after 14 days, unless it has been shared as part of a safety report. The company says it may access the decryption key when investigating a reported safety incident. Uber says that access is limited to that safety investigation.

If a submitted file becomes part of a safety-related report, Uber says it will keep the file according to its data retention policies. So, parents get a live view during the ride, but they cannot go back later and replay the trip.
AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU
Parents can watch their teen’s Uber ride through the driver’s front-facing smartphone camera when live video is enabled. (David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Why Uber is adding live video to Teen Accounts

Uber says Teen Accounts grew from an idea from parents and feedback from drivers. Since launching in 2023, the service has expanded to more than 50 countries. Uber says families now use Teen Accounts for tens of millions of trips every year.
Live video builds on safety tools already available for teen rides. Parents can use live trip tracking and PIN verification. Uber also offers audio recording as another safety feature.

The new video option gives parents something a map cannot provide: a real-time look inside the vehicle. For a parent watching a ride take an unexpected turn or run longer than expected, that extra visibility could be reassuring.
The privacy trade-off parents should know

I can see why this feature will appeal to many families. Watching your teen safely travel across town can offer reassurance that a moving dot on a map cannot provide. At the same time, you are introducing a camera feed into the ride. Parents should understand what happens to that video before deciding how often they want to use it.

Uber says only the linked parent or guardian can watch the stream live. The company also says it cannot access the live feed in real time. However, an encrypted recording can remain on Uber's servers for up to 14 days. Uber says it may access the decryption key when investigating a reported safety incident. That setup gives families more visibility during the ride while leaving an encrypted copy with Uber for a limited period afterward.
Tips for parents using Uber Teen Accounts
Live video can be helpful, but a few simple habits can make teen rides safer from the start.

Check the ride details before your teen gets in. Make sure the driver's name, vehicle and license plate match what appears in the Uber app.Talk about when you will use live video. Setting expectations ahead of time can help your teen understand whether you plan to check every ride or only when something seems unusual.Keep Uber's available safety features turned on. Use live trip tracking and PIN verification alongside live video when those tools are available for the ride.Have a backup plan. Make sure your teen knows how to contact you, reach Uber's safety tools or call 911 if they ever feel threatened or unsafe.
Check the ride details before your teen gets in. Make sure the driver's name, vehicle and license plate match what appears in the Uber app.
Talk about when you will use live video. Setting expectations ahead of time can help your teen understand whether you plan to check every ride or only when something seems unusual.
Keep Uber's available safety features turned on. Use live trip tracking and PIN verification alongside live video when those tools are available for the ride.
Have a backup plan. Make sure your teen knows how to contact you, reach Uber's safety tools or call 911 if they ever feel threatened or unsafe.
It is also worth reminding your teen to trust their instincts. If the driver, vehicle or situation looks different from what appears in the app, they should stay out of the car and contact you.
What this means to you

If your teenager already uses Uber, live video gives you another way to check on a ride without repeatedly calling or texting. Still, I would talk with your teen before the feature becomes part of your routine.

Some parents may want to open the feed only when something seems off. Others may check briefly at the beginning of a ride. The right approach will depend on your teen's age and how much independence your family is comfortable giving them.

Also, remember that live video depends on the driver having the feature enabled. You should still pay attention to the trip details shown in the Uber app. Technology can give you more visibility, but your teen should also know what to do when a ride feels wrong.
RIDESHARE DRIVER ARRESTED IN ALLEGED SCHEME TARGETING IVY LEAGUE STUDENTS FOR SEX: PROSECUTORS
Uber’s new Teen Accounts feature alerts both the teen and driver when a linked parent begins watching the live video. (Photo Illustration by Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
Kurt's key takeaways

I like that Uber is giving parents more visibility into teen rides and alerting both the driver and teen when a parent starts watching. That transparency makes sense when a camera enters the ride. Still, parents should understand the full privacy picture. The live feed ends for the family when the trip ends, while an encrypted recording can remain on Uber's servers for up to 14 days. Uber says it may decrypt that recording when investigating a reported safety incident. For me, live video works best as a tool you can reach for when you need reassurance rather than something you feel compelled to watch for an entire ride. Teens need opportunities to build independence. Parents also need practical ways to respond when something feels wrong.
Would you feel safer knowing you could watch your teen's Uber ride live, or does a camera inside the car cross a privacy line for you? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: What a smart firewall does and why it matters on home Wi-Fi
summary: Router firewalls and software firewalls serve different roles in protecting your home Wi-Fi from unwanted traffic and suspicious connections.
story: Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson warned of worrying privacy clauses in smart devices in a recent episode of the "Beyond Connected" podcast.

Most of us think of home Wi-Fi as the invisible connection that lets a laptop stream a movie, a phone display photos and a printer work from across the room. In practice, it is also the meeting point for many devices, accounts and types of information. A typical home network may include computers, phones, tablets, smart speakers, televisions, cameras, printers and connected appliances. These devices regularly send and receive data.

Some of that traffic is expected, such as opening a bank website or downloading a software update. Other traffic may be unwanted or suspicious. That is where a firewall comes in. A firewall is a security system that checks network connections and applies rules about which traffic should be allowed. Think of it as a doorman for digital connections. It does not know everything about every visitor, but it can help prevent some unexpected traffic from reaching a device.
Understanding how firewalls work, where they fit and what they can and cannot protect against can help you make smarter choices about securing your home Wi-Fi.

FBI SAYS RUSSIAN HACKERS HIJACKED OLD WI-FI ROUTERS

A firewall can help protect home Wi-Fi by controlling network connections, but it works best alongside updated software, strong passwords and backups. (Gavin Roberts/MacFormat Magazine/Future via Getty Images)
Router firewall vs software firewall

Your router is the box that connects your home to the internet and sends Wi-Fi throughout the house. Many home routers include a built-in firewall. Because it sits at the gateway, this router firewall can help protect devices connected to your home network from certain unwanted connections coming from the internet.

A router firewall is useful because one device can provide a basic layer of protection for the network as a whole. It can help reduce direct exposure for computers, phones and other connected equipment. However, its settings and capabilities depend on the router model, its software and how it was configured.

A software firewall runs on an individual device, such as a Windows PC or Mac. It can add another layer of awareness and control at the device level. This becomes especially useful when a laptop leaves home, connects to a different network or needs to distinguish between applications running on that computer.
TRAVEL MISTAKE PUTS PHONE, LAPTOP AND STREAMING ACCOUNTS AT RISK

The two types can work together. A router firewall and a software firewall serve different purposes. The router helps guard the network's front door, while the software firewall helps watch activity involving a particular device.
What inbound and outbound traffic mean
The terms sound technical, but the basic idea is straightforward.

Inbound traffic is data traveling toward your device. For example, a website may send information back to your browser after you request a page, or a remote computer may try to connect to a service on your network. Some inbound traffic is expected, especially when it responds to a connection you started. Other inbound traffic may be unexpected.

Outbound traffic is data leaving your device. Opening a webpage, sending an email, uploading a photograph or syncing a file all involve outbound activity. If an unfamiliar program tries to connect to the internet, that may also be outbound traffic.
CHEAP STREAMING BOX COULD HIJACK YOUR HOME INTERNET

A firewall may use rules, application information and other signals to decide whether a connection looks familiar or requires attention. Depending on the operating system and security product, it may alert you, allow the connection or block it. The goal is to help ordinary online activity continue while making unusual network behavior more visible and manageable.
Why network awareness deserves more attention now

Online banking and shopping place sensitive information at the center of ordinary internet use. You may sign in to a bank, enter a card number, review a medical bill or manage a retirement account from the same computer you use for entertainment.
BEWARE OF HACKERS SHOWING UP PRETENDING TO BE IT

Remote work adds another reason to pay attention. A home laptop may handle work documents, personal files and video meetings throughout the day. If an unfamiliar application begins communicating online, security tools that provide additional context can help you understand what the computer is doing.

A firewall cannot tell whether every website, email or message is honest. A scammer may persuade someone to visit a legitimate-looking page or approve an action that appears convincing. A firewall provides one layer of protection, while your decisions remain an important part of staying safe.
YOUR BANK MAY STOP TEXTING YOU SIX-DIGIT CODES
What a firewall can and cannot do

A firewall can help control certain network connections. It may reduce exposure to some unsolicited inbound traffic and help identify unusual activity involving applications. It can also add a layer of protection when a device connects to networks outside the home.

A firewall cannot make a weak password strong or determine whether someone is being tricked by a convincing text message. It also cannot replace antivirus protection, software updates, multifactor authentication, secure router settings or reliable backups.

No firewall can guarantee that files, accounts or devices will never be compromised. Some threats arrive through activity you intentionally start, such as opening a malicious attachment or entering information into a fake website. Other threats may exploit weaknesses in outdated software. Those situations call for additional defenses and safer habits.
HOTEL WI-FI PHISHING ATTACK TARGETS MICROSOFT LOGINS
Router and software firewalls provide different layers of protection by monitoring connections at the network and individual device levels. (Fabian Sommer/picture alliance via Getty Images)
Home Wi-Fi basics worth checking
A few simple router and Wi-Fi settings can strengthen your home network and reduce unnecessary security risks.

Start with the router. Use the security mode recommended by the manufacturer or internet provider and avoid leaving the administrator password at its default. The administrator password controls important router settings and should be different from the Wi-Fi password.
Install router firmware updates when they are offered. Firmware is the built-in software that helps the router operate. Updates may improve performance, fix problems or address security weaknesses.
Use a strong, unique Wi-Fi password. If your router offers a guest network, consider using it for visitors or devices that do not need access to your main network.
Review the list of connected devices occasionally so you know what is using your Wi-Fi. If you see a device you do not recognize, investigate it and change your Wi-Fi password if needed.

Consider replacing a router that no longer receives security updates or cannot support current security standards. Check the manufacturer's documentation rather than assuming that a newer Wi-Fi label automatically gives you stronger security.
A firewall provides one layer of protection
A firewall works best as part of a broader security setup that protects your devices, accounts and important files.
Keep your operating system, browser, apps and router updated. Turn on automatic updates when that option is available.
Use multifactor authentication for banking, email and other important accounts. Multifactor authentication adds a second verification step, such as an approval on your phone, after your password.

Be cautious with unexpected links, attachments and urgent requests for payment or personal information. Scammers often rely on urgency to get you to act before you have time to question what is happening.
Before approving a remote-access request, confirm who is asking and why. If an alert appears, read it carefully rather than automatically allowing or dismissing it.

Firewalls, antivirus software and backups each protect you in a different way. A firewall helps control network connections, antivirus software detects and responds to malicious software, and reliable backups can help you recover important files if they are damaged, deleted or locked by ransomware. Together, these protections create a stronger defense than any one tool can provide alone.

When choosing antivirus protection, look for real-time malware and ransomware detection, phishing protection, automatic security updates and coverage for all the devices you use. Some products also include device-level firewall protection or cloud backup, but features, storage limits and compatibility can vary by platform.
Visit CyberGuy’s best antivirus protection guide for our current recommendations, comparisons and special offers for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
Protecting the files you cannot replace

Your computer may hold years of family photos, tax returns, medical records, scanned IDs, insurance documents and other files that would be difficult or impossible to replace. That makes protecting your data just as important as protecting the computer itself.

Ransomware is malicious software that can lock or encrypt your files and then demand payment to restore access. A firewall may help block or limit some suspicious connections, but ransomware can reach a device in other ways. Strong security habits and reliable backups give you a better chance of recovering if something goes wrong.

A useful guideline is the 3-2-1 backup strategy: keep three copies of important data on two different types of storage, with at least one copy stored separately from your computer. CISA guidance recommends this approach as one way to improve your ability to recover from ransomware.

Backups work best when they are automatic, current and separated from the same incident affecting your computer. Test a few backed-up files occasionally to make sure you can open them. When practical, keep at least one backup disconnected from your computer or otherwise isolated from routine activity. CISA recommends offline backups because some ransomware can also reach connected storage. Protect cloud backup accounts with strong, unique passwords and multifactor authentication. Norton AntiVirus Plus includes 2 GB of PC Cloud Backup on eligible Windows systems.

If your files suddenly become encrypted, disconnect the affected computer from the network if you can do so safely. CISA recommends isolating affected systems, including disconnecting them from Wi-Fi when necessary, to help prevent the infection from spreading. Avoid rushing to pay a ransom or deleting potential evidence. Preserve messages and notes about what happened and check whether clean backups are available. Consider contacting a qualified cybersecurity professional for help. If you believe an account may also have been exposed, change important passwords from a separate, trusted device.
FCC ROUTER RULE RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT FUTURE UPDATES
Checking router settings, installing firmware updates and reviewing connected devices can help strengthen home Wi-Fi security. (Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)
Kurt's key takeaways

A firewall does a lot of work you may never see, and that is exactly why it can be easy to overlook. Your router firewall helps protect the network at home, while a software firewall can watch connections involving a specific computer wherever you take it. I would use both when available, but I would never count on a firewall by itself. Strong passwords, multifactor authentication, current software, antivirus protection and dependable backups all cover risks that a firewall cannot handle. The bigger point is visibility. Most of us have dozens of connections happening behind the scenes every time we use a computer. A good firewall gives you another set of eyes on that activity and another opportunity to stop something suspicious before it goes further.

title: Fake Chrome update scam could infect your computer
summary: A Chrome extension with 70,000 users and a 4.7-star rating began injecting fake update warnings after a threat actor acquired and weaponized it.
story: Smart refrigerators, cars and computers can show ads after updates, raising privacy and ownership concerns, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson explains.

You are browsing the web when a warning suddenly takes over the page. It says your browser needs a "Critical Update" before you can continue. It looks like Chrome. The message feels urgent. So, clicking Update may seem like the safest thing you can do. That is exactly what makes this fake Chrome update scam so convincing.

Recent reports linked aggressive fake browser update warnings to a Chrome extension called Enable Right Click & Copy - Smart Unlock + OCR. The extension was originally developed as a legitimate tool for restoring right-click and copying features on websites that block them. However, security researchers at Socket now say the extension was later acquired by a threat actor and updated with malicious functionality. It had around 70,000 users when that malicious functionality appeared, although researchers caution that this does not mean every user received the malicious version. The extension was delisted from the Chrome Web Store on Aug. 14 after being flagged as potentially malicious.
FAKE WINDOWS UPDATE INSTALLS HIDDEN MALWARE
Fake Google Chrome update prompts may appear on normal websites and urge users to download unfamiliar files instead of updating through Chrome itself. (David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The bigger lesson goes beyond one extension. Something you installed months ago and trusted every day can change after an update. Here's how this fake Chrome update scam works, how to spot the warning signs and what you can do to protect your browser and computer.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.
