title: Kelly Clarkson Delivers Golden Performance of ‘Most Requested Kellyoke Ever’
summary: Kelly Clarkson went big for her final Kellyoke, saying it’s the “most requested” song: “Golden” from “KPop Demon Hunters.”
story: Kelly Clarkson went big for her final Kellyoke and per usual, it did not disappoint.
Ahead of the last episode of “The Kelly Clarkson Show” on Aug. 31, the host and singer treated fans to a rendition of the “most requested” song she’s received.
The song in question? “Golden” from the hit Netflix animated movie “KPop Demon Hunters.”
The clip begins with Clarkson belting out the first verse of the song, “I was a ghost, I was alone,” before transitioning to the Korean lyrics.
During the final episode, she shared that they taped the performance a few days prior.
The multi-Grammy winner perfectly nails the high notes and makes the song her own as her band accompanies her in the back.
The video ends with Clarkson saying, “That is a very high song.” She added, “I was like, go for it,” and made a face.
Clarkson definitely went for it and the fans loved it.
“Kelly *can do it all* Clarkson strikes again!!!!” one person commented, while another added, “Is there anything she can’t sing?”
Fans also applauded and were impressed that she sang in Korean.
“Also, as a K-pop fan, thank you for taking the time to learn the Korean and including it in the song instead of skipping over it! Amazing!!! It sounded AMAZING!!” one person wrote.
“Of course Kelly Clarkson made sure the Korean she sang was as accurate as possible for a non native speaker. Thank you!” read another person’s comment.

“The Kelly Clarkson Show” is coming to an end after seven seasons. Clarkson first announced the news in February, sharing that this decision “will allow me to prioritize my kids, which feels necessary and right for this next chapter of our lives.”
Clarkson shared 12-year-old daughter River Rose and 10-year-old son Remy with her late ex-husband Brandon Blackson, who died in August 2025.
In a TODAY interview shortly after she announced the end of her daytime talk show, Clarkson told Carson Daly why the timing felt right.

“I think everybody probably gets the timing,” she said Feb. 20. “Our family life, the dynamic changed a bit, and it has changed for a minute now. You got kids, we’ve all got kids, and it’s one of those things when you kind of start seeing life as how precious it is, too. It’s like, ‘You know what, I’m really busy.’”

Clarkson has still kept busy with her Vegas residency, as well as continued to coach on “The Voice.” She’s returning for Season 30, alongside Adam Levine and first-time coaches Riley Green and Queen Latifah, which premieres Sept. 21.

title: Why the Met Gala Just Scrapped its Controversial Theme for 2027
summary: Why did the Metropolitan Museum of Art cancel its tribute to John Galliano? Find out the controversy behind the decision.
story: The Metropolitan Museum of Art and British designer John Galliano announced Aug. 31 that “John Galliano: Horizons,” an exhibition slated to open in May 2027, will not move ahead as scheduled.
That means the Met Gala theme and dress code for 2027, which is always tied to the spring exhibition, will also not be centered around Galliano’s work.

“Following thoughtful discussions with John Galliano, we have together decided not to proceed with the exhibition,” Metropolitan Museum of Art Director and CEO Max Hollein said in a statementannouncing the news.

“After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time,” Galliano said in his own statement, also shared by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
Anna Wintour, a museum trustee who oversees Vogue globally and organizes the Met Gala annually, also provided a statement.

“John’s decision that the exhibition devoted to his work should not take place at this time is very courageous and a measure of the man he is. I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support,” Wintour said.
Here’s what to know about the decision and its preceding controversy.
Why Did the 2027 Met Gala Theme Spark Controversy?
The choice to spotlight Galliano prompted a backlash related to anti-Semitic and racist comments he made in 2010 and 2011, some of which were captured on video.

Galliano was convicted for comments targeting Jews and Asians on two separate occasions at the same Paris bar. At the time the comments were made, he served as Dior’s creative director. He was later fired.

He said in court his remarks were made due to drug and alcohol addiction. Galliano has said that he is now sober. He said his 2024 statement announcing his departure from Maison Margiela coincided with being exactly 14 years sober, per Vogue.

“It’s the worst thing I have said in my life, but I didn’t mean it,” Galliano told Vanity Fair in 2013. “I have been trying to find out why that anger was directed at this race. I now realize I was so f------ angry and so discontent with myself that I just said the most spiteful thing I could.”

According to that Vanity Fair story, “Galliano has spent the last couple of years learning about what he has to do to keep his illness at bay, facing up to what went wrong in his life, and taking certain steps to atone, including reading books on the Holocaust and Jewish history, meeting with Jewish leaders, and reaching out to members of the larger fashion community, including retailers, as part of the process of making amends and possibly returning to work.”
Speaker of the New York City Council Julie Menin blasted the decision in a letter she wrote to Wintour, Costume Institute curator Andrew Bolton and museum director Max Hollein.

“Our cultural institutions, particularly those that receive funding from the City of New York, have a responsibility to demonstrate that hatred and bigotry carry consequences,” Menin wrote in a letter shared with The New York Times. “Words matter, and whom we choose to elevate is a direct statement of our values and what we are willing to tolerate.”

Other prominent leaders from within and outside the Jewish community also criticized the exhibition, while Menin said it was “a gut punch to the Jewish community in our city, who are already reeling.”

“The Met has no tolerance for antisemitism, racism or prejudice of any kind. We are in close consultation with Jewish leaders and other stakeholders, and we take the concerns we’ve heard very seriously,” Hollein told The New York Times.
What Did the Costume Institute Say About its Decision to Change Themes?
Andrew Bolton, curator in charge of The Met’s Costume Institute, spoke to the museum’s decision in a statement.
“I believe deeply in the responsibility of museums to examine difficult histories with rigor, candor, and care,” Bolton said.

“I also recognize the pain and concern this exhibition has caused. After extensive discussion, I support the decision not to proceed. I remain deeply grateful to my colleagues and to the advisors, lenders, collaborators, and community leaders who contributed their knowledge, trust, and perspectives to the project.”

This isn’t the first time the Met Gala has highlighted a controversial figure. The 2023 gala honored the later German designer Karl Lagerfeld, whose comments on women’s bodies, the #MeToo movement and more drew renewed scrutiny.
What Did the John Galliano Say About the Costume Institute’s Decision to Change Themes?
Galliano issued a long statement on Aug. 31 referring to the “debate” around surrounding him, and how it could overshadow the actual Gala.
The statement was also shared on Instagram.

“I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it. I understand that meaningful atonement is not achieved through an exhibition, institutional recognition or a single public gesture. It is a continuing responsibility, demonstrated through listening, learning and one’s conduct over time,” Galliano said.

“I do not want the debate surrounding me to place The Met in a difficult position or to distract from the remarkable work of the Costume Institute. I also recognise and respect that an exhibition honouring my work would be painful for some. I would also like to express my deepest gratitude to all those who have guided, supported and accompanied me throughout these fifteen years of sobriety and recovery from alcoholism and addiction. Your wisdom, patience and humanity have helped me more than I can ever adequately express.”
What Is the New Met Gala Theme?
There is no information on what the new theme will be yet.
In its statement announcing it will cancel the Galliano event, the Met said a new spring exhibition for the 2027 Met Gala “will be announced at a later date.”

title: Are Kayda Bosse and Zach Georgiou From ‘Love Island USA’ Still Together Now?
summary: Kayda Bosse and Zach Georgiou left “Love Island USA” “exclusive.” Here’s what to know about the status of their relationship ahead of the Aug. 31 reunion.
story: To date, or not to date, that is the question— the question Kayda Bosse and Zach Georgiou asked themselves at the end of “Love Island USA” Season 8, that is.

Coupled-up from Week 1, Kayda and Zach’s villa experience was more or less smooth sailing. Aside from the Casa Amor hiccup and Zach’s spat of jealousy over Caleb McDaniel wanting to chat to Kayda, the pair seemed to be happy with their connection.
The real drama emerged at the very end of their summer in Fiji, when a decision to be exclusive — but not boyfriend and girlfriend — upon leaving the villa divided the islanders.
Kayda and Zach secured fourth place in the Season 8 finale.
Ahead of the “Love Island USA” reunion, set to air on Peacock Aug. 31, here’s everything to know about where Kayda and Zach’s relationship stands today.
What Happened Between Kayda and Zach on ‘Love Island USA’?

Zach was part of the batch of original islanders, and on Day 1, he  initially coupled-up with Kenzie Annis. On Day 2, Kayda Bosse and Gabriel Vasconcelos surprised the islanders by pulling anyone who wanted to explore outside their current couple for a “sleep over.”

Kayda and Zach immediately hit it off. Though Bryce Alakai, Zach’s best friend in the villa, was also at the sleepover, he was iced out. That night, there was one giant bed for the three to share, and Kayda and Zach immediately cuddled up together and shared a kiss. When Bryce said he was going to get in on the action, Kayda replied, “You’re going to be left out. Just tonight.”
But it wasn’t just that night, and at the next re-coupling, Zach and Kayda coupled-up for the first time. The pair stayed close throughout their time in the villa.

During Casa Amor, Zach explored a connection with Alannah Keyser, before she was removed from the show on Day 19 after videos surfaced of her using a racial slur. Back at the villa, Kayda got to know Chay Nehra, but was ultimately consumed by thoughts of what Zach was getting up to at Casa Amor. After the girls received a postcard from Casa Amor which depicted Zach and Alannah kissing, Kayda was left in tears, telling Trinity in the dressing room that she felt “so stupid” for thinking Zach would stay loyal to her.

Despite the tears and second-thoughts, both Kayda and Zach went to the Casa Amor re-coupling single and stayed true to their original connection. However, Kayda was unaware that Alannah had been removed from the villa, leaving Zach with no other options. This was brought to light during Movie Night, when Kayda spotted a clip in which Alannah was missing. “Wait, where’s the angel girl?” she asked the other girls. “She left after night two,” replied Casa girl Jaiden Bacciocco, adding “I thought you knew this whole time.”
Kayda confronted Zach, pointing out he had no choice but to stay true to her after Casa Amor. Zach assured her he was always going to stay true to Kayda, and their relationship continued to progress.
Before the finale, Kayda and Zach made things official by establishing they were exclusive.
When Kayda sat down Trinity, her closest friend in the villa, to share the news, Trinity, who was officially Bryce’s girlfriend at this point, asked, “What does that mean?”
“It’s technically like dating, but we’re not boyfriend-girlfriend,” Kayda explained.

Trinity told her friend, “So, you’re in a situationship.” The comment upset Kayda, who had hoped her friend would celebrate the milestone. She received similar lukewarm reactions from the final members of Season 8’s “core four,” Aniya Harvey and Melanie Moreno.

Kayda later told Zach she wished her friends could simply be happy for her. The girls eventually cleared the air during a water park outing in Episode 31, reassuring Kayda they supported her relationship.
Kayda and Zach closed out their “Love Island” experience happily, together.
Are Kayda and Zach Still Together After ‘Love Island USA’?
Kayda and Zach finished fourth in the “Love Island USA” finale, but leaving Fiji presented a new challenge: distance. Kayda was living in New Hampshire, while Zach lived with his family in Australia.

Since then, the couple has closed that gap and made their relationship more official. Kayda shared on TikTok Aug. 19 that she was living with Zach as well as his brother, Charlie Georgiou, who appeared on Season 7 of “Love Island USA.” Kayda also officially called Zach her boyfriend.
Outside of the villa, the couple has been spotted supporting Bryce’s DJ profession as well as partying with influencers such as Tara Yummy.

title: ‘Love Island USA’ Season 8 Reunion Time, How to Watch, Streaming Info and More
summary: What time is the Love Island USA Season 8 reunion? Find out everything you need to know including where and when it will stream, so you don’t miss any of the drama.
story: It has been over a month since “Love Island USA” fans said goodbye to the Season 8 cast during the grand finale, and now it is time to catch up with the islanders to see if the romances and friendships have continued outside of the villa.

A few weeks ago, the cast, including winners Bryce Alakai and Trinity Tatum, the “Core 4” and some divisive islanders came together to film a reunion hosted by Ariana Madix and Andy Cohen. Fans have been waiting to see if rumors about spats between contestants and more tension-filled moments are true. Soon, they’ll get their answers.

Ahead of the Season 8 reunion, Peacock released a teaser that showed Melanie Moreno and Sol Dean bickering, Kenzie Annis seemingly addressing a fallout with Melanie and KC Chandler still harboring resentment for the reactions to his Casa Amor behavior.
Plus, viewers will get to hear updates from Bryce and Trinity and the other finalists about everything that has happened since they re-entered the real world.
Find out everything you need to know about the Season 8 reunion so you don’t miss any of the drama.
When Is the ‘Love Island USA’ Season 8 Reunion?
The “Love Island USA” Season 8 reunion, led by host Ariana Madix and Bravo’s Andy Cohen, will be released on Monday, Aug. 31.
The reunion was taped in front of a live studio audience and it will feature all the OG islanders and bombshells fans couldn’t stop talking about all season long.
Where to Watch the ‘Love Island USA’ Season 8 Reunion
The reunion will stream on Peacock.
The streamer recently announced that “Love Island USA” will return for a ninth season next year with Madix as host.
Peacock previously confirmed that spinoff shows “Love Island: Beyond the Villa” and “Love Island Games” are both returning next year for their third seasons.
What Time Is the ‘Love Island USA’ Season 8 Reunion?
The reunion will be available on Peacock starting at 6 p.m. PT/ 9 p.m. ET.

title: Iran targets American bases after U.S. strikes sites near Strait of Hormuz
summary: The strikes were in “retaliation for the Iranians’ failed attempt at adding sea mines” in the Strait of Hormuz, Trump said on Truth Social.
story: TEHRAN, Iran — Hostilities between the United States and Iran escalated overnight into Wednesday, with Tehran attacking American bases across the Middle East after a U.S. strike was alleged to have hit a home hosting a wedding event, killing five and wounding dozens.

President Donald Trump said in a post on Truth Social on Tuesday that the U.S. had launched a wave of “large and powerful” strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for what he said was a “failed attempt” at laying mines along the vital trade route.

U.S. Central Command, or CENTCOM, said Tuesday it had carried out attacks on Iranian military targets, including air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, communication sites and mine-laying capabilities.

Five people were killed and nearly 70 injured after a U.S. strike on a wedding ceremony in Kuhestak, on the Strait of Hormuz, Fars news agency quoted the Iranian Red Crescent as saying. The regional Red Crescent said at least one child was among those killed.
NBC News was not immediately able to independently confirm the details of the strike.

In video published by the Iranian Red Crescent Society and geolocated to Kuhestak by NBC News, a building can be seen surrounded by rubble, with a gaping hole blown through its roof. Other footage appears to show a downed telecommunications tower just a few minutes’ walk away from the building.
CENTCOM spokesperson Navy Capt. Tim Hawkins said he was aware of reports of civilian casualties.
The “U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC,” he said, referring to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

In response, the IRGC said it had launched a wave of strikes targeting U.S. bases across the region, including in Iraq, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Kuwait.  In a statement, the IRGC said the strikes were in retaliation to the U.S. bombing, which it described as a “flagrant violation of human rights” that turned what it described as an “engagement” event into a “mourning ceremony.”
The IRGC also said had targeted bases in Jordan.

In a separate statement, the IRGC said that four members of its own aerospace forces were also killed in Kermanshah, a city in the central district of Kermanshah province on the border with Iraq, in U.S. strikes overnight, the semiofficial Tasnim news agency reported.
“Make no mistake: these crimes will not go unpunished,” Ebrahim Azizi, chairperson of the Iranian parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, said on X.

If the Islamic Republic retaliates, Trump had warned, “they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings.” When that is over, he added, “there will be very little left” of the country.
The latest bout of violence, which began Sunday with an American bombing of a key island in the Strait of Hormuz, has ended a monthlong lull in fighting between the U.S. and Iran.

title: United States and Iran trade strikes for the first time in a month
summary: Iran launched retaliatory missiles toward Jordan, a U.S. ally, but they were intercepted by American forces, a source said.
story: TEHRAN, Iran — President Donald Trump threatened Monday to forcefully strike Iran after Washington and Tehran exchanged fire for the first time in a month.
“We’re going to hit them hard,” Trump told Fox News, according to the broadcaster’s chief foreign correspondent, Trey Yingst.
Trump vowed there would be “a response” after Iran retaliated to U.S. strikes with an attack on American bases in Jordan.
Trump later told reporters at the White House that the military response would be narrow.
“It’s very limited,” he said, noting that many of Iran’s leaders have been killed and that its navy and air force have been destroyed.
“That doesn’t mean we won’t smack them,” he added.

On Sunday, U.S. forces targeted two rocket launchers on a key island in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. strikes were the first known attack by American forces since late July, and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, or IRGC, said several of its “fighters and compatriots” had been killed and injured.

It was the first major military escalation in weeks in the war between the U.S. and Iran, which began when American and Israeli forces launched a sweeping assault on Iran in late February, killing its supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
U.S. Central Command, or CENTCOM, said on X late Sunday that it had taken “limited” action against IRGC minelaying in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Nepal flood deaths pass 1,100 as hope fades in the search for survivors
summary: The overwhelming stench of death is crushing hopes that more survivors will be found in this Nepali town devastated by last week’s catastrophic floods.
story: BIDUR, Nepal — At the Nepal army staging area in the heart of the flood zone, the roar of helicopters overhead carrying flood aid mixes with the rumble of a bulldozer digging a mass grave.
The overwhelming stench of death is crushing hopes that more survivors will be found in Bidur, a town in Nepal’s Nuwakot district, devastated by last week’s catastrophic floods.
Workers in white hazmat suits unload bodies from a stream of ambulances. They place the wrapped bodies onto a blue tarp in a cordoned-off area.
Helicopters, both military and private aircraft that in better days would be used for commercial tours, take off packed with aid before returning with survivors in need of medical care.
Kalpana Shrestha, a nurse who works in the capital, Kathmandu, is desperate. Ten members of her family are missing — her two sisters and their three children.

“I have shared their photos with journalists, on social media and YouTube, but I have not got any response at all,” she told NBC News in Kathmandu on Tuesday. She added that her loved ones disappeared in Betrawati, a town some 60 miles from the capital that was obliterated in the flooding.
“I have posted so much that my fingers started shaking and trembling,” Shrestha, 35, said. “My mind has stopped working. But even so, we have not stopped posting.”

More than 1,114 have been declared dead in Nepal after last week’s devastating floods, according to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Over 3,916 others are still missing, including at least 583 foreign nationals. In Tibet, at least 16 people were killed and 546 are missing, according to CGTN, China’s English-language satellite news channel.
A State Department spokesperson said Tuesday that 75 Americans remain unaccounted for and that 14 have made their way to safety in Nepal.
More than 10,000 people have been rescued so far, including 252 foreign nationals, the United Nations said.

The disaster, which was triggered by a glacier collapse and landslide on Nepal’s border with China, is now considered Nepal’s deadliest natural disaster since the April 2015 earthquake that killed around 9,000 people.

title: Thousands of U.S. service members arrive in Thailand after record stint at sea
summary: About 5,000 U.S. sailors and Marines are stopping in the resort city of Pattaya for a “rest and relaxation” break as they return home from a record-setting deployment in the Middle East.
story: LAEM CHABANG, Thailand — The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier arrived Wednesday at a port in eastern Thailand, where thousands of U.S. sailors and Marines are disembarking for the first time in more than 280 days after a record-setting deployment in the Middle East.

The toll of the more than nine-month deployment, most of it spent supporting military operations in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, was visible on the carrier as it pulled into Laem Chabang Port in Chonburi province. Paint has worn off and the metal underneath is rusted on the 1,092-foot warship, which is one of the largest in the world.

The Lincoln is in Thailand for a four-day “rest and relaxation” stop on its way home to San Diego after having spent weeks in the headlines as the lengthy deployment raised concerns about supply shortages and the effect on sailors’ mental health.

The U.S. Navy confirmed the ship’s arrival in a statement, saying the Lincoln strike group arrived in Laem Chabang while the destroyer USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. docked in nearby Sriracha and the guided-missile cruiser USS Robert Smalls went to Map Ta Phut in neighboring Rayong province.
The Navy said it was the Lincoln’s first full port stop after 286 days at sea since the deployment began in November.

“Our arrival in Laem Chabang provides a well-deserved opportunity for our sailors and Marines to rest and recharge,” said Rear Adm. Robert E. Loughran, commander of Carrier Strike Group 3. “It also underscores the strong and enduring partnership and alliance between the United States and Thailand.”

About 5,000 sailors and Marines are expected to hit the streets of Pattaya, a nearby coastal resort city that is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Thailand. Each service member will get three “liberty days” and one day of duty aboard the ship, a U.S. military official said.

Upon the Lincoln’s arrival in the morning, service members could be seen working aboard the deck as loudspeakers played announcements about the process for disembarkation. A whistle could be heard ringing across the deck, a Navy tradition that signals coming ashore.
Thai police crackdown on sex workers

Around 1 p.m. local time (2 a.m. ET), service members began disembarking from the ship in civilian clothes, some carrying backpacks. One service member was carrying his golf clubs. Waiting for them across the way were dozens of Ford pickup trucks and buses lined up in columns to take them into town.
“Please be on your best behavior,” a commanding officer could be heard saying over loudspeaker.

Locals in tourism-dependent Pattaya have eagerly awaited the arrival of the Lincoln, which pulled into sight from the shore after sunrise before it made a wide turn and harbored itself at a major cargo terminal.

Officials in Pattaya, where international tourist arrivals have dropped because of travel disruptions and soaring fuel prices stemming from the conflict in the Middle East, say the visit is expected to inject about $3 million into the local economy.

Authorities in Pattaya have stepped up security, with heightened police patrols and checks along the roads. Businesses here are also trying to woo the sailors, with some putting up banners to welcome them.
Wichai Yuankham, 35, a factory worker who came to watch the ships arrive, said the naval visit was a welcome boost to the local economy.
“I am just excited to see the destroyer docking,” he said. “This is my first time seeing the destroyer, and I feel good seeing it, and we can boast to our neighboring countries about this.”

title: Allies bristle as sanctioned Russian finance minister attends U.S.-hosted G20 summit
summary: Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov was left out of the “family photo” of finance ministers at a G20 meeting after complaints from Ukraine’s allies.
story: ASHEVILLE, N.C. — Traditionally the “family photo” of finance ministers at a G20 meeting is a dull, grimacing group clad mostly in gray. But this year’s picture may be much more interesting for some because of whom it omits.

Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov — who was sanctioned by the United States in April 2022 — was left out after complaints from some of Ukraine’s European allies as he attended his first Group of 20 summit on U.S. soil since President Vladimir Putin invaded his neighbor four years ago, NBC News has learned.

Having served in the role since 2011, Siluanov is widely considered to be one of Putin’s most trusted Cabinet members. But he was given the cold shoulder by some of those in attendance at the event in Asheville, North Carolina, although he addressed the summit and met with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Bessent told NBC News on Tuesday that he brought up “with everyone that we have implemented our economic outcast policy, and that we expect everyone to come along with us.” He was referring to sanctions he introduced last week targeting countries and international entities facilitating trade with Iran.
Asked about Siluanov’s response, Bessent said: “Many conversations are best done privately.”

But a source familiar with the meeting told NBC News on Monday that Bessent, who sanctioned Russia’s two largest oil companies in October,  had made clear to his counterpart the “U.S. will not provide Russia with economic relief until the war in Ukraine is over.”
When Siluanov tried to discuss areas of interest, Bessent “forcefully interrupted and said nothing is possible until the war is over,” the source added.

The pair met on the sidelines of the forum, with the discussion focusing on “Russian-American cooperation,” the Russian Finance Ministry said in a statement on its website. The ministry did not immediately react to NBC News’ request for comment about Siluanov’s omission from the “family photo.”

Siluanov’s presence appeared to rattle some of Ukraine’s European allies, including German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil, who said the signal sent ​by ​receiving the ⁠Russian finance minister in the U.S. was “quite troubling.”

title: Record baby boom brings world’s heaviest parrot back from the brink
summary: A record 90 chicks have been added to the population count of the kakapo parrot in New Zealand, delighting conservationists.
story: There’s been a baby boom among one of the world’s most endangered parrot species — and officials in New Zealand are squawking about it.
A record 90 chicks have been added to the count of the endangered kakapo parrot, bringing the population to a record 325 birds, the New Zealand Conservation Department said in a statement Tuesday.

The fledglings of the bird, which is native to New Zealand, were bred this year. The youngest is now 150 days old, a milestone at which the baby birds are considered independent enough to be added to the tally.
And every bird counts.
The green parrots do not fly and have a waddling gait, making them an easy target for ground predators. The kakapo is also the heaviest parrot species, with males weighing up to 9 pounds.

The bright birds, with finely blotched yellow-green plumage and large gray beaks, are also thought to be among the longest‑living bird species, reaching 60 to 90 years, the statement from the department said.
The nocturnal parrots with their owl-like faces remain critically endangered, conservationists say.

“There is still a long road of recovery ahead, but ninety chicks in a single season is a record. In the early years of recovery, it took 16 years to produce that many chicks,” said Deidre Vercoe, manager of the department’s kakapo recovery operations.

“We had a four-year gap between breeding seasons, so it’s fantastic to finally see the population increase,” she said in a statement. “It’s also a significant milestone for the species, as the last time the population is thought to have exceeded 300 birds may have been as long as 75 years ago.”

The Kakapo Recovery Programme began in 1995 with a population of just 51 birds, including only 20 females. Since then, the species has been through 13 breeding seasons, with recovery efforts working to overcome challenges associated with low genetic diversity, including infertility and poor hatching success. The successful season also highlights the importance of creating more predator-free habitats for the species.
Each kakapo in the program is fitted with a small backpack radio transmitter to help track its location and monitor its activity levels, conservationists say.

title: Thieves steal royal necklace from Vienna museum in smash-and-grab heist
summary: The robbers, who didn’t disguise their faces and were caught on camera, remain at large with the 673-diamond necklace once owned by an Egyptian queen, police said.
story: Austrian police are searching for a pair of brazen thieves who made off with a diamond necklace — once owned by an Egyptian queen and worth millions — by smashing a display case at a Vienna museum in broad daylight.
But unloading the hot rocks stolen last week from the Museum of Applied Arts, known as MAK, could be their undoing, art heist experts said Monday.

“Just like with paintings, it’s hard to sell well-known pieces of jewelry,” said Anthony Amore, a Boston-based art theft expert and investigator. “The Catch-22 is nobody will buy it intact. So it would not surprise me if their aim is to take the piece apart and sell the jewels individually.”
Robert Wittman, who once led the FBI’s Art Crime Team and is now a security consultant, agreed.
“What I expect they aim to do is pop the diamonds out of the settings and melt it down,” he said.
If they do, they will dramatically reduce the value of a one-of-a-kind piece that Sotheby’s auction house in New York sold in 2015 for $4.3 million, the experts said.

“They’re better thieves than businessmen,” Wittman said. “What gives this piece its value is not just the diamonds, but the provenance, the history of the piece. They take this piece apart and they’ll be lucky to get a couple hundred thousand, if that.”
That’s if the thieves can find a buyer for the baubles, the experts said.
“Anybody who knows anything about diamonds is going to know where these diamonds came from,” Wittman said.

The robbery bore little resemblance to jewel heists depicted in movies like “The Thomas Crown Affair” or “Ocean’s 8.” The thieves didn’t scale the walls after hours or short-circuit the security system to get inside the museum.
Instead, according to police, they bought tickets, strolled in with their faces uncovered and made their way to an exhibition of works from the French luxury jeweler Van Cleef & Arpels.

There, the 200-carat platinum necklace encrusted with 673 diamonds, which once belonged to Queen Consort Nazli of Egypt, was on display. She wore it at the 1939 wedding of her daughter and Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, the future shah of Iran, according to the museum.
The thieves managed to get a hammer past security and used it to smash the glass case, grab the jewels and flee, police said.
The museum’s surveillance system caught the whole thing on camera, police said.
The Vienna State Police Directorate is asking the public to help identify the culprits, whom it described as slim men with dark hair and short beards.

The experts interviewed by NBC News said the Vienna robbery is the latest in a string of high-profile heists that have hit European museums, including the theft in October of French crown jewels and other items valued at $101 million from the Louvre in Paris.

“The thieves didn’t disguise themselves perhaps because they knew camera placement and quality,” Amore said. “With the advances in security technology, I fear we might see thieves turn to brute force more frequently in the future. Museums must prepare themselves for this, because they are all targets.”
Wittman said top-notch museum security requires good equipment, good guards and good procedures.

“It’s like a three-legged stool,” he said. “One leg goes and the stool tips over. Obviously, in this case, they didn’t have good human resources. I mean, the thieves were able to grab the necklace and get away.”
That having been said, Wittman said he’s confident the robbers will be found. He’s not so sure about the fate of the necklace.
“I expect it won’t take long before they know who they are,” he said of the thieves. “Hopefully, they’ll catch them before they melt this piece down.”

title: Death toll in Nepal floods tops 900; number of missing nearly doubles to more than 4,200
summary: Rescuers continue to struggle to reach communities days after the massive flooding that stemmed from a glacier collapse.
story: More than 900 people were killed by the devastating flooding in Nepal, officials in the South Asian country said Monday as the number of those listed as missing almost doubled to 4,247, including 592 foreign nationals.

The government “has mobilized all available resources and efforts at its disposal for search, rescue, and relief and recovery operations,” a spokesperson for the Nepali Foreign Ministry told a news conference Monday, before thanking a number of countries, including Qatar, the United Kingdom, Australia and Japan, for helping out with relief efforts.
“So far, 903 bodies have been recovered,” the spokesperson said, adding that 10,000 people had been rescued, including 323 foreign nationals.
Separately, Nepal’s disaster agency said 4,247 people were missing as of 1 a.m. ET Monday. On Saturday, the country’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, put that figure at 2,400.

title: Bootleg ‘Spider-Man’ swings into Russian cinemas despite Hollywood boycott
summary: While screening the movie “violates both Russian and international law,” everyone, including Russian authorities, “turns a blind eye to it,” one film critic told NBC News.
story: “Spider-Man” fans dressed up as their favorite web-slinger have swung into cinemas across Russia to see the latest installment of the franchise, despite Sony Pictures ending all of its theatrical releases in the country at the start of the war with Ukraine.

Wearing a homemade costume with the iconic spider symbol drawn onto a red shirt, Almir, 27, was among the hundreds who flocked to the cinema to watch “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” in the city of Kazan, which sits around 500 miles east of the capital, Moscow.
“I did it myself, since I didn’t have money for a full suit,” he told NBC News in a Zoom interview last week, adding that demand for tickets was so great that he had to book three weeks in advance.

NBC News agreed not to use Almir’s last name and those of other moviegoers because they were nervous about potentially landing themselves in trouble with authorities for speaking to a foreign media organization.

But while screening the movie “violates both Russian and international law,” everyone, including moviegoers, owners and even Russian authorities, “turns a blind eye to it,” according to the film critic Timur Aliev.

“Formally, a cinema has no right to screen a film without a distribution certificate,” Aliev said. But these were impossible to obtain, as most of the major Hollywood studios had closed down their distribution offices in Russia after the start of the war, he said.

title: Sen. Ted Cruz calls for elections in Venezuela to proceed ‘rapidly’
summary: The Texas Republican also said the U.S. should arm protesters in Iran.
story: Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Sunday renewed his call for free and fair elections in Venezuela, just two days after the Trump administration announced that the U.S. would take over 65 billion barrels of oil from the South American nation.
“There need to be democratic, free elections in Venezuela,” Cruz told NBC News’ “Meet the Press,” adding later in the interview that elections should take place there “midway through next year.”
The acting Venezuelan president, Delcy Rodríguez, took over after U.S. forces captured then-President Nicolás Maduro in January and brought him to the U.S. to face drug-trafficking charges.

“Delcy Rodríguez was Nicolás Maduro’s vice president,” Cruz said Sunday. “Maduro was illegitimate. He was a Marxist. He had seized power contrary to the will of the voters, and from the beginning, I have been urging, and I believe the administration is working towards this, that there should be free and fair elections.”
The senator also praised the oil deal announced on Friday that will allow the U.S. to take control of 65 billion barrels of oil reserves from Venezuela.

“The oil deal as announced sounds like it could have a very positive impact on the United States and the United States economy, on American jobs, and a very positive impact on gas prices over the long term,” Cruz said, adding that he doesn’t think the U.S. needs to prioritize free and fair elections in Venezuela over the oil deal.

“I don’t think the timing matters as much as the one versus the other. I think the oil deal will move as rapidly forward as it can,” he said. “But I think free and fair elections need to proceed, and they need to proceed rapidly. I believe they should proceed no later than midway through next year.”
The Trump administration, the senator added, is “working rapidly to do that.”
Earlier this month, Cruz joined a bipartisan group of senators in introducing a resolution affirming the United States’ support for free and fair elections in Venezuela.

Cruz also spoke Sunday about the ongoing U.S. military conflict in Iran and called on the Trump administration to arm Iranian protesters to achieve a goal of “regime collapse” in the Middle Eastern nation.

“I would like to see the longer-term objective be regime collapse,” Cruz said, adding later: “What I’ve been urging is for President Trump and the Trump administration to arm the protesters, so that the people of Iran ... remove this regime from power. Not American boots on the ground, but the Iranian people.”
Days earlier, President Donald Trump posted an image on Truth Social declaring “mission accomplished” in Iran.
On Sunday, the senator said the “initial mission” in Iran — degrading the nation’s military capacity — was complete, but called for the removal of the ayatollah as a secondary objective.

Cruz also spoke about his presidential ambitions, which sparked headlines this week after he told MS NOW in an interview that the GOP has not automatically chosen Vice President JD Vance as President Donald Trump’s successor.
“There’ll be time to figure that out,” the senator told MS NOW, adding, “I’ll certainly be part of the discussion.”
Asked directly about whether he’s seriously considering a presidential campaign in 2028, Cruz said Sunday that he would make a decision after November’s midterm elections.

“The Book of Ecclesiastes tells us there’s a time for every season. This is not that season right now. This is the season of the midterms, and I’ll tell you, I’m spending my time on the road, campaigning for candidates all over the country,” the senator said.
“There will be a time for that conversation” about running for president, he said later in the interview.
Trump praised Cruz on Thursday when asked in the Oval Office about the senator potentially running for president in 2028.
“I would say that he’s very talented. He’s a very good friend of mine. I think he might do that, yeah. He’s a very — he’s a talented guy,” the president said.

Ten years ago, Trump and Cruz faced off in the Republican presidential primary as major foes. Trump went on to beat Cruz to win the GOP nomination and the presidency, but along the way delivered a stream of insults against Cruz, his father and his wife.

title: Fears of more flooding in Nepal, 100 Americans among the missing as rescue efforts step up
summary: Nepal’s Flood Alert system warned heavy rain could raise water levels in some areas, prompting fresh alerts for residents along waterways.
story: KATHMANDU, Nepal — Authorities in Nepal have warned of the risk of further flooding after heavy rain, as China sheds light on the scale of the disaster in its Tibet region.

Five days after surging floodwaters from a glacier collapse buried communities across the region in thick mud, rescuers in Nepal were still struggling to reach devastated communities as the full scale of the destruction emerged.

“The disaster here is overwhelming,” Ferrin Cole, an operations director at the U.S.-based Crisis Response International, told NBC News on Sunday. “The flood that came down that mountain just wiped out cities. We’re going in as fast as we can to get people the help that they need.”
Cole said that his team would be working to help locate missing people but that working in mud “is actually pretty dangerous.”
“The longer that death and mud are together, diseases breed, and so we’re always just aware of that,” he added.
Approximately 100 Americans are among the missing across Nepal and China’s Tibet region, the State Department said Saturday.
How did the catastrophic Nepal-Tibet flood happen?

In Nepal, the death toll has risen to 781, with over 2,500 people still missing, including 592 foreign nationals, according to the country’s disaster agency. The Nepal Tourism Board said 289 foreign nationals have been rescued.

China has separately reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing in its Tibet region, including 261 foreign nationals. It is unclear how much overlap there is between the Chinese and Nepali missing-person counts.

Those missing loved ones may face a long wait for answers, with many bodies washed far downstream and recovered in poor condition. Morgues in Nepal have been overwhelmed, though authorities are collecting DNA samples in the hopes of notifying relatives.
In Nepal’s Chitwan district, where a number of bodies have washed up, police officer Anil Thapa told Reuters that “more than half” of recovered bodies were “beyond recognition.”
“Many have no visible faces. In some cases, only hands or legs remain,” the officer added.

The response is also being complicated by a landslide-dammed lake above the border checkpoint that is overflowing, while heavy rain in Nepal has pushed up river levels and prompted fresh warnings for people living along waterways.
Nepal’s flood alert system said Sunday that heavy rain had been measured in various watershed areas of Gandaki province, and that the water levels were “expected to rise.”
“Therefore, people living in riverside areas are requested to adopt caution,” it said on X.
But in flood-hit areas, residents were struggling to make sense of repeated warnings since the initial floods.

“Sometimes they say a flood is coming, then we have to run again to higher ground, even at night. There is also rain,” Govind Shreshta, a resident of the town of Galchhi, told The Associated Press. “It’s really difficult for me. I have a 72-year-old father and 70-year-old mom. I must carry them and I am exhausted. It’s going on like this for those who are still alive.”

Chinese state-run media outlet CCTV said Sunday that the event was part of a growing pattern of glacier-related disasters in the region, with the avalanche reaching China’s Gyirong Port within minutes of occurring.
“The disaster was caused by glacier instability resulting from the long-term effects of climate warming,” said Chinese state media.

“It struck suddenly, with a large peak flow, high speed, severe destructive force and a wide impact area,” the report added. “These are also new and significant characteristics of cryosphere-related disasters emerging across the Tibetan Plateau and surrounding regions.”
While it will take time to determine the exact cause of the mudslide and flood disaster, analysts say climate change likely played a role.

The Himalayan region, which includes Nepal, India, Pakistan, Bhutan, China and Afghanistan, is among the places most vulnerable to climate change, with temperatures rising faster than the global average. The warmer conditions are accelerating glacial melt, further destabilizing a region that is already prone to floods, landslides and earthquakes.
The suspected collapse of a melting glacier shook the ground so violently that seismic monitors initially registered it as a magnitude-4.4 earthquake.

The U.S. Geological Survey later revised that number to the equivalent of a magnitude-5.2 earthquake and said a second seismic event three hours after the first registered as the equivalent of a 4.2 temblor. Debris flow and flooding from what it called a “slope failure” traveled 62 miles, the USGS said.

“We will not be able to attribute 100% that this is because of climate change, because these changes have been happening” over a long period of time, Neera Shrestha Pradhan, an expert at Nepal’s International Center for Integrated Mountain Development, said Friday. But climate change might be breaking a threshold, she said, and “maybe that might be one of the causes of this happening.”
Janis Mackey Frayer, Dawn Liu and Sunil Pandey reported from Kathmandu and Freddie Clayton from London.

title: Nepal flood death toll rises to more than 700 as nearly 2,500 remain missing
summary: The death toll from catastrophic flash floods and mudslides in Nepal rose to at least 734 on Saturday, as nearly 2,500 people remained missing in the country, including about 100 Americans.
story: The death toll from catastrophic flash floods and mudslides in Nepal rose to at least 734 on Saturday, as nearly 2,500 people remained missing in the country, including about 100 Americans.

More than 8,100 people have been rescued, according to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, which consolidates information from Nepal Police, Nepal Army and Armed Police Force. More than 90,000 people have been affected by the disaster, according to the Nepal Red Cross.

Rescuers have struggled to reach devastated communities along the Nepal-Tibet border, with the scale of the disaster coming into view four days after the torrent of water, ice and debris swept through Himalayan valleys, destroying homes, bridges and other infrastructure.
As families wait for news about their relatives, damaged roads, power outages and fears of further flooding have hampered rescue efforts.
Of those missing in Nepal, 589 are foreign nationals, according to the disaster agency. The Nepal Tourism Board said 261 foreign nationals have been rescued.
House nearly engulfed by Nepal floodwaters

China has separately reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing in its Tibet region, including hundreds of foreigners. It is unclear how much overlap there is between the Chinese and Nepali missing-person counts.

The disaster began Wednesday when a massive chunk of ice and rock dozens of times larger than the Empire State Building broke off a mountaintop and triggered the catastrophic flooding, geologists said.
Videos from the hardest-hit border regions showed people running as the debris flow swallowed buildings and vehicles, devastated towns and settlements, and severed roads, power and communications.

The suspected collapse of a melting glacier shook the ground so violently that seismic monitors initially registered it as a magnitude-4.4 earthquake. The U.S. Geological Survey later revised that number to the equivalent of a 5.2 magnitude earthquake and said a second seismic event three hours after the first registered as the equivalent of a 4.2 temblor.
Debris flow and flooding from what it called a “slope failure” travelled 62 miles, the USGS said.

The State Department said Friday it is not aware of any confirmed American deaths, but the large number of U.S. citizens still unaccounted for has added to the growing uncertainty surrounding the disaster. Approximately 100 Americans remain missing, while five have been rescued, the department said Saturday.

Among the missing are Murphy, Texas, residents Raghu Rajan and Archana Suresh. The pair were expected to cross the China-Nepal border Wednesday morning when the floods hit. Their phones last pinged that morning near a bridge that washed away.
“We know the severity of it, but still, you know, there’s a ray of hope for us to find our loved ones,” Rajan’s sister-in-law Divya Chandrashekar told NBC Dallas-Fort Worth.

Deepak and Madhu Ahuja, Plano, Texas, business owners who have been married for 34 years, were in the area for a religious journey to Mount Kailash, a sacred site for both Hindus and Buddhists. Their family is now desperately trying to find them while holding out hope that they survived.
“My first reaction was, ‘That cannot be true,’” Deepak’s brother Sushil Ahuja said. “They went there for a good cause, right? This cannot happen to them.”
The State Department has urged U.S. citizens “currently in, or recently traveling through Rasuwa or another affected area” to get in touch via KathmanduACS@state.gov.
A spokesperson said relatives seeking information about family members in Nepal “should call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free from the United States and Canada, or 1-202-501-4444 from other locations.”
On Saturday, helicopters resumed operations in Nepal’s flood-hit Nuwakot district after poor weather temporarily halted efforts.

Some helicopters arrived loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice, while others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors, among them several babies from the nearby community of Trishuli.
Meanwhile, China’s Ministry of Emergency Management urgently dispatched five tunnel experts to join rescue efforts at a hydropower station tunnel in Nepal, Chinese state media reported on Saturday.
Scores of bodies recovered along the banks of the Trishuli and Narayani rivers have been brought to the city of Pokhara on Phewa Lake in central Nepal for identification.

At the Western Regional Hospital in Pokhara, a crowd of families gathered Friday outside the facility’s morgue as they anxiously waited to see if their loved ones might be among the dead being brought to the medical facility.
Inside the hospital, a digital display could be seen being set up to show photographs of the faces of some of the victims, in hopes that their loved ones might be able to identify them.
The display was set up by police, with authorities saying some of the bodies recovered from the floods were in an advanced state of decomposition, making physical identification difficult.
China’s state-run media, CCTV, said the most significant risk facing search-and-rescue crews is a landslide-dammed lake above the border, where a barrier has started to overflow and release water.
“It is currently stable overall, and the likelihood of a complete breach of the landslide-dammed lake is relatively low,” CCTV reported.
Rescuers are working “day and night” to search for survivors amid challenging conditions, a U.N. official said.

“The government has established a relief fund, and already the World Bank, India, China and the U.S. have committed to pledge $229 million to support,” Lila Pieters Yahia, the U.N. resident coordinator in Nepal, said, adding that the U.N. is also providing $2 million from its humanitarian relief fund for immediate assistance.
Nepal may need $4 billion to $5 billion to rebuild following the disaster, the country’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle told Reuters on Saturday.
CCTV attributed the flooding to the effects of global warming.
“The disaster was caused by glacier instability resulting from the long-term effects of climate warming,” it said.
It said monitors showed a span of seven minutes between the avalanche and its impact on Gyirong Port, the hard-hit border crossing with Nepal.

“It struck suddenly, with a large peak flow, high speed, severe destructive force and a wide impact area,” CCTV said. “These are also new and significant characteristics of cryosphere-related disasters emerging across the Tibetan Plateau and surrounding regions.”

title: Palestinian woman and NBC News team attacked by masked Israeli settlers in West Bank
summary: The woman and the crew were treated for injuries. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence committed “by a handful of rioters.”
story: Masked Israeli settlers attacked and injured a Palestinian woman and members of an NBC News team reporting in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Saturday.

Three members of an NBC team were interviewing Aida Ahmed Abdullah and her family in the Palestinian town of Jalud, near Nablus, when the attack occurred. Abdullah said they had been driven out of their home by Israeli settlers, and the team was walking down a hill toward the house.
A gray car with Israeli license plates then drove in reverse up the hill toward them, video of the incident shows.

A masked man in a blue tracksuit, holding a stick, was leaning out of the rear passenger window as the vehicle approached. When the car stopped, at least four men in dark clothes and with their faces covered leaped out, hitting Abdullah and the crew with sticks and throwing rocks at them.
“They jumped out, beat us, then jumped back in the car,” said NBC News international correspondent Matt Bradley, who was hit twice in the arm and later treated at a nearby clinic.

Abdullah, 51, who was on the ground after the attack, was taken for medical care by the Red Crescent. Her injuries were not life-threatening, according to an Israeli military and Israel Border Police statement. According to her husband, Mahmoud Toubasi, Abdullah’s condition had improved but she remained in the hospital Saturday night.
Two additional members of the NBC News team — a cameraman and producer — were also injured and were treated following the attack.
Producer Lawahez Jabari described how the car rushed up the hill before its occupants beat members of the team and damaged camera equipment and one of the crew’s vehicles.
“Suddenly a car came to us,” she said after receiving medical care. “The settlers had sticks. I saw a gun, but they didn’t use the gun.”
Camera operator Khaldoon Eid, who lives in the West Bank, said he was surprised the attack occurred in the middle of the village.
“We didn’t expect that — that they would come to attack,” he said. “We were in the middle of a Palestinian area next to Palestinian houses.”
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his spokesman Doron Spielman condemned the violence against Abdullah and the NBC News crew along with several other incidents across the area on Saturday.
Those incidents included dozens of masked Israeli settlers spraying pepper spray at Palestinian workers and throwing rocks at a building in nearby Qusra.

Netanyahu said the “criminal acts of violence committed in the villages of Kosra and Jalud by a handful of rioters who violate the law, cause enormous injustice to the law-abiding settler public, hinder the IDF in fulfilling its missions and harm Israel’s standing in the world.”

Spielman said in a post on X that “their actions violate the law; they endanger both Jews and Arabs, and they interfere with the Israel Defense Forces as they carry out vital security missions, and of course they harm Israel’s international legitimacy.”
Netanyahu, he said, requested that security forces “apprehend the perpetrators and to bring them to justice,” adding Israel “will not tolerate vigilantism of any kind by anyone.”

Israeli security described the regional violence on Saturday, saying they received reports that “rioters had arrived in the area and that violent clashes had occurred, including stone-hurling toward Palestinians and additional civilians.”
“Upon their arrival, the security forces identified dozens of rioters who had barricaded themselves inside a Palestinian home while Palestinian residents were inside,” the statement said.

“The security forces who arrived at the scene initially operated to remove the rioters from the home and separate the groups, in order to protect the residents inside the house. In addition, the security forces confiscated vehicles belonging to the Israeli rioters that were suspected of having been used to reach the area,” the statement said.
“IDF soldiers and Israel Border Police forces continue to operate in the areas of Qusra and Jalud to prevent further disturbances and restore order in the area,” it added.
There has been a spate of Israeli settler violence in the West Bank, and the village of Qusra has been besieged by Israeli settlers for weeks.

Between Jan. 1 and July 24, Israeli forces or settlers killed 76 Palestinians, according to the latest data available from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. Three Israelis were killed over the same period, the data shows.

Netanyahu’s hard-line government has been accused of turning a blind eye to the settler attacks in the West Bank, which many governments around the world consider illegally occupied. In its statement after the attack, Israeli security forces said they “strongly condemn all forms of violence.”
Captured in the 1967 Middle East war, the West Bank is home to 3 million Palestinians and 500,000 Israeli settlers.

The recent escalation in violence has increased pressure on the Israeli military to stop these armed groups. The United Nations and media workers have also reported an uptick in attacks on foreign, Palestinian and Israeli journalists in the West Bank.

title: Trump says U.S. has struck deal with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of oil reserves
summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that the U.S. had entered into an agreement with Venezuela to take control of the country’s 65 billion barrels of oil reserves.
story: President Donald Trump announced Friday that the U.S. had entered into an agreement with Venezuela to take control of the country’s 65 billion barrels of oil reserves.

“BREAKING NEWS: The United States of America has just entered into an Agreement with the Country of Venezuela on, THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY! At my direction, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, working closely with Highly Respected Interim President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, and, through a partnership with private business, have secured majority U.S. control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
Trump added that the transaction “MORE THAN DOUBLES American Oil Reserves.”
In January, the U.S. military carried out an operation to capture Venezuela’s President Nicolás Maduro to face federal narcoterrorism and drug trafficking charges in the U.S.
Trump is facing increasing pressure as the midterms loom and gas prices have spiked because of the war with Iran, which the U.S. and Israel started exactly six months ago.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio touted the deal as a “huge win” for both the U.S. and Venezuela in a post on X.

“It demonstrates how President Trump’s bold foreign policy is driving America First wins: securing stable reserves and low-cost oil in our Hemisphere and lowering gas prices here at home,” he wrote. “For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs, and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela’s economy.”

Venezuela has among the largest oil reserves in the world, with an estimated 303 billion barrels of crude oil in the ground. That’s about 17% of the world’s supply, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Unlike other parts of the world, where geologists have to search for untapped oil, the reserves under Venezuela’s soil are largely mapped and known, experts say. But because of dilapidated infrastructure, the country only produces about 1% of the world’s oil.

title: Families wait in agony as Nepal floods leave hundreds missing
summary: A New York couple traveling to Mount Kailash is among 65 Americans missing after a catastrophic flood along the Nepal-Tibet border.
story: The last time Radhika Sharma heard from her parents, they had just crossed from Nepal into Tibet.

Ramesh Sharma, 65, and Neelam Sharma, 64, who live in New York and are U.S. citizens, were making a religious pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, a peak in Tibet considered sacred by Hindus, Buddhists and other faiths. Shortly after their border crossing Wednesday, a towering torrent of water, rock and mud tore through the same Himalayan corridor.

Videos from the hardest-hit border regions showed people running as the debris flow swallowed buildings and vehicles, devastated towns and settlements, and severed roads, power and communications. The suspected collapse of a melting glacier shook the ground so violently that seismic monitors initially registered it as a magnitude-4.4 earthquake.

In one video from Mailung, in Nepal’s Rasuwa region, a group of construction workers was seen walking down a mountain path before noticing giant plumes of brown debris in the distance, rapidly cascading toward them. The men reversed course to flee uphill, one briefly stopping to film before realizing the scale of the danger.
He shouts in Nepali: “Oh, my God, the flood is getting so big! Let’s run — run fast, guys! Oh, my God, get back quickly!”

As of Friday morning local time, authorities had recovered 469 bodies in Nepal and confirmed three deaths in Tibet. Hundreds more remained unaccounted for. Nepal’s Tourism Board said 644 travelers, including 65 Americans, were missing.
Sharma’s parents were among a group of seven people making the journey to Mount Kailash, visited by tens of thousands of pilgrims each year.
“It has probably been the worst 24 hours of my life,” Sharma, 32, a doctor based in North Carolina, said in an interview as she continued an anxious wait for news.

The hardest part, she said, was the not knowing. She has contacted the U.S. embassies in Nepal and China, as well as American officials domestically. “I haven’t heard anything back,” Sharma said initially, although later added that embassy officials in Beijing had been in regular touch with her.

After posting pleas on social media, Sharma has been put in contact with people in Nepal “who are trying to help track down my parents,” she said. “I’ve given them my parents’ information, their photos. I’m on the phone now, just waiting to hear someone say that they’ve even seen them.”
Sharma is far from alone in desperately seeking information about loved ones.

The State Department has urged U.S. citizens “currently in, or recently traveling through Rasuwa or another affected area” to get in touch, and encouraged loved ones of those missing to contact U.S. officials via various means.
It was “working closely with local tour agencies and local authorities to assist Americans in the affected areas. Nepali-led search and rescue operations continue,” a State Department spokesman said.

As of 2 p.m. ET Thursday, it was aware of 90 Americans who may have been “impacted” by the floods on the Nepal-China border. Three American citizens had been safely rescued by that time, the spokesperson added.

Add to Google
In Baidur, Nepal, Shova Shrestha, 33, has spent more than a day waiting for news of her missing husband, Rajan Shrestha, as rescue efforts continue.
“I keep looking at each helicopter, hoping he will step out of it,” she told The Associated Press.
Sagar Pandey, chief executive of the tour company escorting travelers from Australia, India, the U.S., Canada and Singapore, could only assess the devastation where they had been from a helicopter.
“There are no human-made things, no human settlement left. Everything is just flat,” he told Reuters. “So anyone in the hotel, the restaurant or the car, I believe that everybody is gone.”
Syed Sadique, who runs a tour agency based in southern India, was waiting anxiously for news on the fate of 57 people traveling with his company, including his tour guide son, Sayed Umar Farook.

“The group ⁠was traveling on three buses in Nepal,” he told Reuters. “A member of the group told us that one vehicle carrying about 20 people managed to get through safely, while passengers saw another bus plunge ​into a gorge.”
Amid the carnage and chaos, and her desperate outreach to authorities and locals, Sharma sent a message to her missing parents themselves.
She said she told them: “I love you. I am looking for you. I will keep looking for you. I  just hope you’re OK.”
Sharma added: “I know that wherever they are, they’re probably a lot more worried about my brother and I, because that’s just the type of people they are.”

title: Harry and Meghan arrive for ‘extended’ stay in the U.K. six years after royal exit
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan arrived back in the U.K.  after six years in California, a source close to the family confirmed to NBC News.
story: LONDON — Prince Harry and his family sought to begin a new life for a second time as they arrived back in the United Kingdom on Wednesday after six years in California, a source close to them confirmed to NBC News.
The Duke of Sussex, 41, and his wife, Meghan, 45, flew in on a private plane with their two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, according to several media reports.

A spokesperson for the Sussexes declined to comment on where the family would be living, citing privacy and security concerns. However, the spokesperson did confirm that they brought their dogs with them, although their chickens would remain in Montecito, California, where the family had been living since 2020.
A source close to the couple told NBC News last week that they were moving back for an “extended period” of time.
Harry and Meghan rattled the British royal family six years ago when they opted to step down as working royals, eventually choosing a quieter life in the affluent coastal enclave in Santa Barbara.

Relations have been strained in the years since, worsened in part by explosive allegations of racism and bullying made by the couple in their Netflix documentary “Harry & Meghan” and in Harry’s memoir, “Spare.”
After years with few signs of a royal rapprochement, Britain was shocked last week when it emerged they were planning a return.

Harry and Meghan will remain private individuals and nonworking members of the royal family, a source familiar with the couple’s plans told NBC News last week, while reports in British media indicated that Archie and Lilibet have been enrolled in schools in the country.

Questions remain over what security arrangements will be in place for the couple, after a protracted legal battle between Harry and the British government over the removal of their security protection.
Asked about their security last week, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: “This is a private matter, it’s a matter for Harry and Meghan, and we wish them well in the moves that they’re making.”

The couple’s planned return had sparked a slew of media coverage, with front pages dominated by unconfirmed reports that Meghan could return to acting for the first time since she departed the television show “Suits” ahead of her 2018 wedding to Harry.

Harry’s return to Britain also comes after he and several other claimants were ordered to pay a combined £34.5 million ($46 million) to a major newspaper publisher after losing a High Court battle over alleged breaches of privacy. That battle was one of several salvos between Harry and the British press.
